batches.family: Authority review intake route and store (0C.1 REV)

batches.family: F01 Cron, scheduler and job results: one scheduled-job manifest, POST-only routes, one cron-secret rule, honest job results

items.explanation: All four aliases export POST only; so do the other ten scheduled routes (codemod f01-cron-post-only.cjs, idempotent). A contract test fails if any manifest route exports a method other than POST.

The manifest declares all 18 scheduled routes; apps.bicep generates one Container Apps schedule job per entry (POST with the cron secret, curl -f so a non-2xx fails the run). Compiles with az bicep; the contract test fails when a cron route is missing from the manifest or the bicep stops reading it.

One shared rule (x-cron-secret or bearer; CRON_SECRET_KEY then CRON_SECRET; unset never matches) used by withApi, verifyCronAuth, the rewards route and the edge check, which now compares in constant time over SHA-256 digests via WebCrypto (edge-safe) instead of !==. CRON_API_ROUTES is derived from the manifest.

The vercel.json entry (no method, no secret) is removed; calendar-sync is scheduled as a POST Container Apps job every 15 minutes, and verifyCronAuth now accepts the secret as a bearer token as well as x-cron-secret.
location-retention is an hourly POST Container Apps job generated from the manifest.

The route's own Authorization-only CRON_SECRET-only check is replaced by the shared rule, so one transport (x-cron-secret) satisfies the edge and the route; the edge compare is constant time; the GET handler is removed.

The calculation catch now records, logs and returns the failing organization; the save step returns the failing organization ids; the route answers 500 with counts and ids through jobResponse when any failed, and no longer runs markOverdueRemittances a second time.

An unknown task is a 400 that runs nothing; a rejected organization, an organization that resolves with success false, and an expiration batch whose own flag is false are failures; the run answers 500 naming the scopes; rejected errors serialise as text instead of {}.

The handler answers 500 for a run with any failed source and for the outer failure; every sync method writes the log row through syncLogOutcome: partial (not completed) when records failed, with the bounded collected error list in error_details.
billing-lifecycle is now a daily POST schedule job.
items.remaining: The route's generator still needs a session, so it cannot run headless; that needs its own review.

items.explanation: A run with failed session-reminder or expiry-warning sends answers 500 through jobResponse naming the failed batch, with the sent/failed counts and collected errors in the body; the message no longer claims success. The route writes nothing, so it is classified as a read-only POST for the audit ratchet.

batches.family: F01 Provider webhooks: Resend delivery events applied by rules, once, in one transaction

items.explanation: An event matching neither a message_log row nor a delivery-ledger row answers 404 retryable so the provider redelivers (covering an event that beats the sender storing the provider message id); a redelivery after the row exists applies it. Both are tested against PostgreSQL (pglite).

Status only advances to a higher rank (a late sent, delivered or opened never overwrites bounced, failed or complained); fact timestamps are filled when missing; existing metadata is preserved. The table comment no longer claims the log is immutable and states the real rule. Mutation-proved.

Each statistic counts a message at most once (a counted set persisted in message_log.metadata, seeded from timestamps and terminal status for older rows), and the campaign counters advance inside the UPDATE (jsonb || jsonb_build_object over the stored value) rather than from a value read earlier. Tested with redelivery and with a counter another writer already advanced. Mutation-proved.

A complaint or suppression now creates the preference row when none exists, writes a revoked consent record and the audit entry, and applies once per message in the same transaction. A complaint or provider suppression now ends the recipient's subscriptions to the organization's own distribution lists as well as its preference, and is recorded platform-wide in a governed mechanism: platform 0053 adds email_address_suppressions (SHA-256 of the address only, no plaintext; cache 0043 makes it SYSTEM_ONLY), the webhook writes it in the same transaction as the consent record and the audit entry (only when the event names exactly one recipient; several are not guessed), and the single sending function refuses a suppressed address from any organization and fails closed if the list cannot be read. It is a delivery suppression, not consent, so other organizations' consent records are untouched. A platform administrator lifts one only through an audited route (reason required, row kept); a later complaint clears the lift. Proven on native PostgreSQL 15 and 16 and against a real SQL engine through the webhook.
items.remaining: Only lib/email-service.ts is gated; any other code that talks to a provider directly would bypass the list (none was found).

items.explanation: recordProviderCallback takes the caller's transaction (inserting inside a savepoint so a duplicate does not abort it); the webhook runs it in the same transaction as the message row, so a ledger failure rolls everything back and the retry repeats nothing. An unmatched or ambiguous ledger result is logged, and an event matching nothing is retried. Rollback proved with a failing audit write.

Migration 20261031 creates a unique (provider, provider_message_id) index when no pair repeats, otherwise a plain index with the duplicate count reported; both branches and idempotence executed on PostgreSQL (pglite). The webhook locks the row (FOR UPDATE) and refuses with 409 when two rows carry the id. Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

batches.family: F01 Provider webhooks: Shopify redemption lifecycle - one code format, shop-bound organization, retryable and idempotent, proportional refunds, no purchaser data

items.explanation: The code issued and the code parsed are defined together (shopify-redemption-rules): UE plus the 32 hex characters of the redemption id, lossless. The parser also accepts the dashed form and resolves a legacy 12-character code only as a prefix inside the shop's organization among redemptions awaiting payment, and only when exactly one matches, so codes already issued still complete. Round trip unit-tested; the full paid, fulfilled, refunded lifecycle runs against PostgreSQL (pglite).

A failure answers 500; an event that cannot be applied yet (a fulfilment or refund for an order not recorded as paid) answers 503 with Retry-After; neither records a receipt, so the redelivery is applied. A receipt is recorded only after the handler, only for a final outcome, and tolerates a concurrent duplicate. The handlers are idempotent on their own state (an order already applied is a success), so the separate receipt transaction cannot lose or double-apply an event. Mutation-proved.

A refund returns its share of the credits (floor of creditsSpent x refunded line-item subtotal / order line-item total), a later refund returns its own share, each Shopify refund id is applied once, the redemption becomes refunded only when everything spent has come back, and the total returned never exceeds the credits spent. Refunds are recorded in the stored payload and in the audit entry. Mutation-proved.

The receipt keeps only the topic, shop domain and the order or refund id; the redemption keeps order facts (number, currency, totals, product and variant ids, quantity, price) and no customer id, e-mail, name or line-item title; discount codes are no longer logged. Migration 20261102 irreversibly redacts what was already stored in webhook_receipts and reward_redemptions (executed on PostgreSQL pglite, repeatable).

Every lookup and write of the handler runs inside withRLSContext bound to the shop's organization, and the redemption's organization is checked against it. The organization comes from the shop domain through migration 20261101: a unique index on the lower-cased domain and a column-level SELECT (org_id, shop_domain) grant with a read-only policy for the system role; the token and secret references stay unreadable (executed with real roles and RLS on pglite). The runtime-role behaviour under the real application roles is still to be qualified on native PostgreSQL.

The shop domain header must belong to exactly one organization or the signed event is refused (403, logged), each shop has its own rate-limit allowance, and the pre-signature limit is keyed on one normalised address instead of the whole forwarded-for string.
items.remaining: The HMAC still uses one global SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET for every organization; per-organization secrets (shopify_config.webhook_secret_ref) need the secret store. The address key is only as trustworthy as the front proxy that sets the header.

batches.family: F01 Scheduled jobs that alert or import: durable deduplicated alerts, one transaction per alert, paged and leased imports

items.explanation: The in-process bus events are replaced by a durable inbox alert for the steward each late or at-risk claim is assigned to, written inside that organization's own context and deduplicated by a unique index over (organization, user, claim+kind+deadline) from migration 20261103: a rerun, retry or overlapping run adds nothing; a new deadline or escalation alerts again. Unassigned claims are counted in the result. Real-SQL tested; mutation-proved (dedupe, recipient). Native PostgreSQL qualification of the migration is still to run.

The scan is keyset-paged (500 per page, bounded page count that fails the run rather than truncating silently), each claim is assessed once, and the metrics are awaited with their failures reported through the job result (500 naming the organization). Metrics are keyed by organization and clock hour.
items.remaining: recordPilotMetricEvent does not deduplicate by trace id, so two runs in one hour still record two metric rows; an idempotency key needs support in @nzila/platform-pilot-metrics.

items.explanation: The rule, inbox notices, execution record and audit entry are all written on the sweep's transaction handle in one savepoint per signal (the module-level db handle is no longer used for writes). Proved on PostgreSQL: an audit failure leaves no inbox row and no execution for that alert while other organizations' alerts are kept, and the next run completes it.

The never-read pending notification_tracking row is no longer written and an execution records only the channel that delivered (in_app, with the recipient count) and its measured time. The alert goes to the organization's active administrators and president; an alert nobody can receive is a failed execution and a failed job (500), not a success. Reruns in the same hour alert nobody twice. No e-mail is sent or claimed; delivering alerts by e-mail is not part of this fix.

The Google import follows every page (250 per call, 50-page bound that fails instead of truncating), the cron passes the stored sync token (without the window and ordering Google rejects with one), a 410 falls back to a full sync, and the new token is stored only when every page was read and every event applied; otherwise the import throws and the connection is recorded as failed with a retry time. Per-event and token-store errors are no longer swallowed. The due connections are locked FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and leased for 15 minutes in the same transaction, each lease bound to the row's organization. Google only: the Microsoft import has the same shape and is not yet changed.

batches.family: F01 Rewards cron: atomic per-member awards, honest scheduled and expiration tasks, organization context and run audit

items.explanation: Repeat protection (an advisory lock per organization and award type, and a same-day NOT EXISTS over the member's awards in any state) was already in the source and is proven on PostgreSQL by anniversary-idempotency.pglite.test.ts (existing, not mine). What was still open is closed here: each member's create and issue is one savepoint, so a failure in either rolls both back and no approved award is left un-issued, one member's failure no longer aborts the others' work in the shared transaction, and the run reports failed members (success false) instead of a smaller count. Proved on PostgreSQL: a failed issue leaves no award for that member and the next run completes only that member.

The unused years-of-service scale and its helper are removed (credits are the award type's configured amount, which issueAward applies); the years are recorded in the award metadata. The reason text names the organization (read inside the transaction) instead of its UUID, tested on PostgreSQL. No years-of-service credit scale is applied: that would be a product decision on money, not a fix.

A scheduled rule names an award type and a cron expression but nothing that says who earns the award, so no award can be derived; the task now reports those rules as skipped (and logs a warning) and never as processed. Evaluating scheduled rules remains unbuilt; it is not claimed.

The three overlapping windows are replaced by exact-day tiers (30, 14 and 7 days out), so a daily run warns each earning once per tier; the warned amount is capped at what the member still holds and spent credits are not warned; a failed send makes the batch fail and is counted per organization. Proved on PostgreSQL and mutation-proved.
items.remaining: There is no sent record, so two runs on the same day (a retry, an overlap) mail the same member twice, and a missed day misses that tier; a durable per-earning-and-tier sent marker needs a table. Nothing in the product sets an expiry or writes an expire entry yet, so the task still has nothing to warn about.

items.explanation: The cron lists organizations under system authority and runs each organization's anniversary and scheduled task inside that organization's own RLS context, so the services' shared db handle is subject to row-level security on that path.
items.remaining: The wallet and redemption routes wrapped by withRoleAuth, and the expiration scan (a cross-organization read), still reach the shared handle without a tenant context; each needs its own routing.

items.explanation: Each organization's anniversary and scheduled run writes an audit entry (processed, failed or skipped, success) inside its own context, the organizations whose members were e-mailed get an audit entry with the sent and failed counts, an audit that cannot be written fails the run naming the organization, and a member's create and issue are one atomic unit.

The score is presented as a rule-based heuristic: no confidence, no interval and no training date are returned or stored. Same: 410 with no data body, upstream's change, existing test.

batches.family: F02: organization figures, report engine, signature, social analytics, satisfaction and settings answer from stored records or refuse

POST stored a snapshot whose summary said synthesis was pending and whose themes, positions and recommendations were empty. It checks authority and then answers 501; nothing is stored. The snapshot list is unchanged.

The route served a table no route writes and nothing enforces under the name of an employer data firewall. It answers 501 and the table's governance entry was removed. items.remaining: A credentialRef is still accepted and stored and nothing resolves it to a secret; a vault-backed resolution path does not exist.

items.remaining: Native PostgreSQL 15/16 under real tenant RLS, exact-HEAD full unit/contract execution, HTTP/browser/staging proof, and audit/financial-mandate qualification are still outstanding. No independent CLOSED credit.

batches.family: F11: model output is shown as what it is: no canned reply stored as a model answer, no value typed into a provenance field, scoring before limiting, and feedback that counts a case once

items.explanation: A create answers 501, so no AI reference id, confidence score or data source can be typed into a stored insight. The only change a person makes is a triage (acknowledge, start, complete, dismiss with a reason) on an existing insight, stamped with their identity and the server clock, guarded by a transition table and a status predicate, and audited in the same transaction. The panel's PATCH, which had no route behind it, now has one.
The weekly summary is a deterministic seven-day aggregate that says so (aiUsed false, no AI reference, no confidence) (upstream's change, existing test and contract).
Embedding cache statistics need platform system-administrator authority and are audited (batch B18).

A failed generation raises ChatbotUnavailableError (a 502 from the route) and stores nothing; it no longer saves a canned apology as an assistant message from the model "fallback". Test disclosure: the test that asserted the stored fallback was replaced. The ai-client mock lacked buildOrgAiTrace, so the other sendMessage tests had been passing on that canned reply; the mock now provides it and those tests exercise a real generation.

The search scores a bounded candidate set (500 rows) and applies the requested limit to the best matches; a row with a missing or unreadable embedding is skipped instead of throwing; a threshold of 0 is honoured.

The model row is locked for the read-modify-write; a prediction is scored once (409 on a repeat); feedback no longer creates a model under a version the caller names (404), and a prediction that records its own version is scored only against it.
items.remaining: The SLA prediction rows written by the prediction route carry no model version column, so the version binding applies only where the stored prediction has one.

items.explanation: The body is parsed with a typed, bounded schema: purpose, description and text are non-empty bounded strings and the two allowance flags must be booleans (a string "false" was stored as consent); an invalid or non-JSON body is a 400 that records no consent.
items.remaining: The consent text and purpose are still supplied by the client; a server-owned notice with a version the member acknowledges needs a client change.

items.explanation: The monitoring alerts route answers 501 (batch B15); no literal drift value or per-second alert id is returned.
The same route answers 501, so there is no acknowledgement to key on an id alone.
The churn-risk route answers 501 (batch B10); no member is profiled from case history.
The program enrolment item answers 501 for every method, so a program id can no longer rewrite or delete a training course.

batches.family: F04: a generic CRUD route names the fields a body may write and the columns a response omits, and a path that the factory cannot serve answers 501 instead of refusing every request under another name

items.explanation: A create accepts an allow-list that excludes certification, representation, status and count fields, and a PATCH blocks them; they have no source yet.
items.remaining: No dedicated route records a certification or changes representation, so those fields are unwritable until one exists.

items.explanation: Notes and custom fields are omitted from every unit response.
The site manager's name, e-mail and telephone, the notes and the custom fields are omitted from every worksite response.
The assessment (premium rate, assessable payroll, premium due) is read at the officer floor.
The WCB claim routes answer 501 explicitly instead of refusing every request through the governance denial; the table no longer has a generic route and its governance entry was removed.
The feed answers 501; it was the generic factory over the communications campaigns table.
Both routes answer 501 (they were the factory over external accounts under a labour-board name, refused for every caller).
The API-key route answers 501 explicitly: no key is issued, listed or revoked through it.
The onboarding root answers 501 instead of refusing every form submission through the governance denial of the pending-profiles table.
A report body writes only name, description, type, category, configuration and template reference; creator, counters, last run, organization and template flag are the server's.
The bulk member route answers 501 for POST and GET rather than reporting an operation it never performed (upstream's change).
The update-role route answers 501 and returns no roster rows (batch B09).
The role-repair route answers 501 at the system-administrator floor and no roster is exposed (upstream's change, existing test).
The person who holds the phone registers it at the member floor, every row is the caller's own, and the token is never returned (batch B02).
The storage routes answer 501 (batch B15); no caller-written media row is inserted.
The per-capita remittance ledger is DENIED for every generic read and write, and the tax paths no longer read it (upstream's change, existing test).
The slip, RL-1, T106 and COPE receipt paths answer 501 (upstream's change); a slip is not issued by any route.

batches.family: F03: a reference in a body names a row of the caller's own organization or is refused, and a read over joined or hierarchical data stays inside the caller's organization

items.explanation: A clause create verifies that the agreement belongs to the caller's organization (404 otherwise) and that any parent clause is a clause of the same agreement, and accepts only author fields: the embedding, hash, confidence, extracted entities and counters are processing outputs.

The employer and worksite ids taken from a unit or worksite body are checked against the caller's organization on create and update (400 malformed, 404 not the organization's). Test disclosure: the two worksite route tests that pin the factory options now expect the reference hook.

Every joined table is bound to the caller's organization inside its own ON clause, and a join must follow a declared relationship; proven on real SQL for non-equi, LEFT, RIGHT and FULL joins (upstream's change, existing test).
The route returns only the caller's own live roles; it is no longer the generic factory over the unscoped profiles table (upstream's change, existing test).
The survey, its responses and its questions are all read with the caller's organization predicate (upstream's change, existing test).
The unscoped shared item is written only at the platform content-manager floor, so an organization administrator cannot change it by id (upstream's change, existing floor test).

The organization list resolves the caller's read authority (active membership, an administered ancestor, or platform) and returns a projection under explicit scope instead of relying on the connection role; proven on real SQL (upstream's change, existing test).
A malformed parent or status filter is a 400 before any read, and the list is bounded at 1000 rows (existing test).
items.remaining: The administration pages still treat the list as the union's organizations for choosing a parent; for a caller with no ancestor authority it is only their own row.

items.explanation: The search is limited to the organizations the caller may read and exposes member counts only to administrative readers (upstream's change, existing contract test).
The tree and hierarchy read the system context only after resolving the caller's readable organization ids, and are bounded (upstream's change, existing contract test).
The reset needs a system administrator, a pilot or demo runtime and an explicit confirmation naming the organization (upstream's change, existing test).
items.remaining: Seeded rows still carry no demo marker, so a reset deletes by organization and slug rather than by marker.

items.explanation: Dispatch assignment verifies the request and every worker id against the organization with the request locked, proven on real SQL (batch B12).

batches.family: F12: route-specific defects already repaired in source, credited only where an existing or new test pins the repair

items.explanation: A registration forces the member identity and the registered state and ignores every client-sent completion, payment, attendance, grade, certification and subsidy field; its course and session must belong to the organization (upstream's change, existing test).

A certification is created only from a completed, passed registration of the organization for a course that issues one, as a pending candidate with no verifier, verification date, badge or certificate URL (upstream's change). Only a source contract pins it; the route has no behavioural test.

The analytics route answers 404 to a caller with no read authority over the organization named in the path and is officer-level for those who have it (batch B11 and upstream, existing tests including real SQL).

The OAuth state is an unpredictable signed value bound to the browser, provider, user and organization, expiring, carried in an HttpOnly cookie and verified before any token exchange; it fails closed without a signing key (upstream's change, existing test).

batches.family: F05/F06: inputs are typed and bounded, commercial data is read by those who administer it, effects are audited with their record, and retained records are ended rather than deleted

items.explanation: A contract create checks that its billing account and subscription belong to the caller's organization (400 malformed, 404 otherwise) before anything is written; a contract provisions entitlements from its lines. B76: amounts are decimals with at most two places, the expiry must follow the effective date, a line total must equal unit price times quantity, a stated total that disagrees with the priced lines is refused, and the line count (100) and text lengths are bounded.
Contract list and line items are read at the officer floor.
Subscriptions are read at the officer floor and paused or resumed by an administrator (was a steward).
items.remaining: Authority is still a role title with the financial-mandate check only on reconciliation; subscription changes need the live financial mandate.

items.explanation: Timesheet GET and POST now require the explicit financial-member role allowlist and a live principal financial mandate within the authenticated organization transaction. GET enforces finance:view and scopes rows to employers covered by the grant (bounded to 200). POST requires finance:prepare scoped to the employer before any registry read or insert, and preserves organization checks, bounded CSV, duplicate refusal and same-transaction audit.
items.remaining: Exact-HEAD behavioral/unit and contract execution, native PostgreSQL 15/16 with real RLS and mandate fixtures, HTTP/browser/staging qualification, and institutional mandate issuance remain outstanding. The route stays PARTIAL and no CLOSED credit is claimed.

items.explanation: The keyword search puts the sensitivity floor in the query so the limit counts only readable interviews, treats LIKE wildcards in the query as literals, and reads nothing when no level is allowed. Test disclosure: the drizzle mock gained inArray and one test was added.

List and item reads are restricted to the pension financial administrator role, bound to the tenant, paginated and audited (upstream's change, existing test). This is an engineering restriction, not an issued trustee mandate.
Amendment and deletion of trustee meetings are refused until a versioned amendment and retention workflow exists (upstream's change, existing test).
T4A generation answers 501 and stores nothing (upstream's change, existing test).

DELETE now terminates the plan (status and time) and keeps the row and its enrolments, contributions and claims; a repeat is 409 and a foreign plan 404, audited in the same transaction. Test disclosure: the route had no test, so none was replaced.

Transcription is rate limited per caller, requires an organization context, and records the disclosure (language, size, type; never the audio or text) before the recording leaves; if the audit cannot be written nothing is sent.
items.remaining: There is no entitlement or consent decision for sending a recording to the external service.

items.explanation: The collection reads and writes run through the public-intake guard (rate limit; body cap on writes). Claimed-workbook writes were already audited.
items.remaining: The per-holder item route is not yet behind the guard, there is no per-workbook holder cap, and unclaimed-workbook reads are not audited.

items.explanation: Distribution lists and their subscriber e-mail addresses are read at the steward floor, and the subscriber list is bounded to 5000 rows. Test disclosure: the subscribers route test's mock chain gained limit.
Rewriting an integration's endpoint and field mapping needs an administrator, as the delete already did.

Contract create, activate and terminate write their audit record in the same transaction (persistAtomicAudit) instead of a separate best-effort logger call. Test disclosure: the service test now mocks persistAtomicAudit in place of the logger.
The system-context counter update names the organization of the row that was read.

batches.family: F12/F06: a check states only what it verified, an aggregate never runs without an organization, and an administrative record is read and written as exactly that

items.explanation: The strike-vote and certification checks no longer return compliant, warning or violation from numbers the caller typed against thresholds written into the route; each reports the arithmetic, says no validated rule is configured and that the figures are unchecked, as info. Test disclosure: one test added; the existing tests did not assert a verdict.
The literal thresholds are removed and there is no rule lookup to swallow.
The response carries the number of checks evaluated and, when none applied, a notice that this is not a finding of compliance.
The organization audit records are read at the administrator floor, tenant-scoped, bounded to 100 and read-audited (upstream's change, existing test).
items.remaining: The read still returns the whole audit row; a field projection for the administrator view is not defined.

items.explanation: A manual entry is recorded as compliance.manual_entry attributed to the administrator who wrote it, with the declared fields kept as untrusted details, so it cannot pass for a system record (upstream's change, existing test).

batches.family: F12: a record moves through its lifecycle by rule, the server owns its status and counters, and a route reads the id from the path segment it is mounted on

items.explanation: A campaign create accepts author fields only, and a PATCH blocks status, send times, delivery statistics and the audience count; campaigns are read at the steward floor because they carry segment queries and bodies.

A survey moves draft, then active or published, then closed, never backwards; the server stamps the publication time once; response counts, views and completion are never client-written and a new survey cannot be created already published.

The poll item route was mounting the collection handlers (GET and POST), so no poll could be read, changed or removed by id; it is now an item route on [pollId] with the same lifecycle guard, and the vote totals are blocked from PATCH.
The schedule and send-test paths answer 501: they were the campaign row under another name and no sender reads them, so nothing was scheduled or tested.
items.remaining: No sender exists: schedule and send-test answer 501 and nothing reads a campaign to deliver it, so the audience, communication preferences and consent are not evaluated by any send path; the consent check belongs to the sender when one is built. A campaign row remains a draft record whose scheduledAt and sendImmediately fields are intentions only.

items.explanation: Anonymous callers receive only the build identity; the environment, host, deployment type, feature profile and image digests need the deployment-probe credential, always with no-store (upstream's change, existing test).

The full operation inventory is served only to an authenticated administrator and never cached by a shared cache; the public documentation is the reduced openapi.json (upstream's change, existing tests).

batches.family: F09/F10: a financial write is rate limited and repeatable without piling up records, an endpoint validates the request it actually performs, and an exported package states only what the data supports

items.explanation: The duplicate path was the generic CRUD item over message templates (its DELETE removed the template and nothing was duplicated); it answers 501 and the roster-facade ratchet pins it.
Every pension write (create plan, enrol member, update plan, terminate plan) carries the financial-write rate limit; the contract test checks each write configuration.

The cancel path now validates a cancellation (redemption id and a bounded reason, strict) and uses that validated id; an initiation body is rejected with 400 instead of being parsed and discarded, and the reason is stored with the cancellation. Test updated: the previous cancel test posted an initiation body and a query id, which is the defect.

A replay identical in run, mode, rule version, engine version and result is answered with the replay already made, adding no replay row, artifacts, evidence link, compliance event or audit duplicate; a different requested mode is a new replay. Tests added for both.
items.remaining: A genuinely different replay still opens an error-severity event that must be acknowledged before approval; whether a replay should gate approval is a payroll-governance decision, and replays are still allowed at any run status.

items.explanation: The requested mode and replay rule version are stored with the diff, so an engine-change replay can be told from a faithful re-run.
items.remaining: The mode enum column still holds only exact and simulated; adding new_engine needs a PostgreSQL enum migration that has not been run on a native database.

items.explanation: The uploaded external employee id is neutralised against a leading formula character and quoted in the remittance CSV, and each remittance group reports the number of members who contribute to it rather than the payroll item count.
items.remaining: The per-group member count is pinned by source only; no behavioural test drives the remittance route with a zero-amount group.

items.explanation: Validation failures are classified as validation (not unauthorized access), every evaluated result has a tenant-bound atomic audit receipt, and the route fails closed with 503 when the audit cannot commit (existing implementation, existing tests).
The invoice create path answers 501 stating that invoices are ingested from the provider; the contract test pins that it never inserts.

batches.family: F03: a record is read under the organization that holds it, a shared record under what its own row permits, and a platform read of other organizations is attributed and recorded first

items.explanation: A replay first requires a live financial view mandate for the run (resource-scoped, as the run detail does) and only then reads any payroll item. Tests adapted: assertions that no transaction was opened now assert that nothing is written, because the mandate check is itself a transaction; the not-found test asserts the mandate was requested. New test: a role holder with no mandate is refused before any read.

The remittance run detail needs the financial roles and a live view mandate for the run, reads inside one tenant RLS transaction, and returns only the evidence manifest, never the stored CSV or JSON (existing implementation, now pinned).

A new readCondition option applies to every GET whatever the caller's role; both decision routes use it so a decision marked not public, or carrying an access restriction, is neither listed nor returned. The precedent service behind the search, list and by-id reads applies the same restriction (B33). Platform 0051 gives the library an owner (source_organization_id, recovered from typed provenance where it names a real organization) and defaults is_public to false; cache 0041 forces row security so a tenant reads a decision that is public with no access restriction or one it supplied, and writes only rows it owns. An ownerless decision changes only through the system role. precedent-service create, update and delete are owner-scoped and run in the tenant transaction, and a read no longer counts itself (view_count is not maintained). Proven on native PostgreSQL 15 and 16 under the runtime and system roles.
items.remaining: The combined bootstrap still creates arbitration_decisions as a Django stub: the remaining Drizzle columns are the separate schema-parity item, so the library routes still need that shape before they work against a real database.

items.explanation: The clause and bargaining-note reads take the caller's organization as a required argument and name it beside the agreement id, so a child row written against another organization's agreement is never returned. Existing service tests adapted only by passing the new argument; the route test now asserts the notes read carries the organization.

A completion is a locked transition of an existing registration of the organization that must be attended and passed, audited in the same transaction; nothing is inserted (existing implementation, now pinned).
The path no longer mounts the generic factory over pending_profiles; it answers 501 and exposes nothing (existing implementation and test).
The onboarding root answers 501 instead of mounting the factory over pending_profiles, and the roster-facade ratchet pins it.

The precedent item route reads under the caller's tenant context with an explicit sharing check, and PATCH and DELETE name the owning organization in their own WHERE clause and audit in the same transaction (existing implementation, existing pglite isolation test).

A GET never links or rewrites a membership by e-mail address or through another user id's profile; memberships are only those already bound to the caller (existing implementation, existing tests assert no update).

The platform user directory and activity feed record the read under the system scope before running it and refuse (409) if that record cannot be written; the search term is bounded with LIKE wildcards taken literally, and the activity limit is a bounded integer.
items.remaining: Authority is still the platform_lead role title rather than a mandate, and both reads still return member names and e-mail addresses across every organization by design.

batches.family: F06: a precise position or interview text is recorded or sent onward only after the consent and configuration checks, and a telemetry read stays in the caller's organization

items.explanation: A geofence entry still answers inside or outside for the point the caller supplies, but a geofence_events row is stored only when the member holds a valid opt-in (the strike permission for a strike fence) and tracking is enabled; the response states whether anything was recorded. Existing test adapted: the opted-in case now queues the consent and configuration reads; three new tests cover no consent, tracking disabled and a missing strike permission. Verified later: checkGeofenceEntry stores a position only when the member has a valid opt-in (with the strike permission for a strike fence) and tracking is enabled.

The publication decision gates expertise extraction by the interview's level and consent, the AI call is bracketed by requested, completed and failed audit records, and the result update is limited to the published row (existing implementation and tests).

The expertise map, topic graph, propagation map and timeline aggregate only published, consented interviews of the organization at the levels the caller may read, proven against a real SQL engine (existing implementation and tests).

Reads of the interview and of its knowledge-base copy apply the interview's current consent and sensitivity, so a withdrawal or reclassification takes effect on the next read (existing read-gate tests).
items.remaining: The knowledge-base row, its content and its embedding are not erased or deactivated when consent is withdrawn; they are only filtered at read time.

items.explanation: The three platform financial metrics answer 501 with a NOT_IMPLEMENTED capability state and no figures (existing implementation and test).

A pilot telemetry read uses the caller's authenticated organization; a request naming another organization is refused 403 identically whether or not it exists. The resolver had no test; it now has one, and each route is pinned to use it. B76: the services no longer run on the bare handle: each read runs inside the tenant context of the session organization, so the row-level policy applies as a second boundary.

Publishing now needs the officer floor instead of the steward floor; the publish is already rate limited and bracketed by intent and outcome audit records. B85: POST /api/social-media/posts now only records a draft for each named account (account_ids is required and each account must be an active account of the organization on a selected platform), with its audit record in the same transaction; nothing is sent. A different officer approves or rejects it at POST /api/social-media/posts/review (the author cannot; a rejection needs a reason): the approval is claimed atomically before anything is sent, the external publish is audited before and after, the post is completed in place, and the deciding officer and time are kept on the post. The publish tests that pinned an immediate publish were rewritten for the draft flow (disclosed) and a review-route test file was added.

batches.family: F12: a job runs statements the schema declares, a read states a failure as a failure, an acknowledgement means the record exists, and a removed record is no longer read or counted

items.explanation: Both reminder statements now name only columns the training schema declares (start_date, venue, lead_instructor_name, certification_number, the organization_members row that carries the name and e-mail) and join every table on the organization; they run against tables created from the declared schema, with positive and negative cases (cancelled, inactive, revoked, other organization). Route test adapted only to the new row field names.

British Columbia now has an open-ended top tier at the statutory maximum of eight weeks, and a test asserts that every jurisdiction ends in an open tier and that tiers are contiguous and non-decreasing. The lower British Columbia tiers were not changed here; they were not checked against the statutory text.
The rules route serves the board as a reference with verification required and no deadline number under an arbitration category (existing implementation and test).

A new strict lookup throws on a failed or timed-out query (and clears its timer); the profile route answers that as a failure, and says no profile exists only when the lookup completed and found none. The tolerant lookup remains for callers that treat failure as no profile.
The contact form answers 503 instead of ok when the CRM did not record the contact or the message, so a visitor is no longer told it was received when nothing recorded it.
items.remaining: There is still no local store: a submission exists only in HubSpot, and an unconfigured CRM refuses every contact submission.

items.explanation: A failed alert or report query answers 500 instead of an empty success, and both lists are bounded to 500 rows.

Queue counts and failed task names are for the control-plane key or a platform administrator and refuse a signed-in member (existing implementation; the contract test pins the administrator check before the queue read).
A missing stored creation, update or join time is returned as null rather than the time of the call.
All six vocabulary routes serve a signed-in response with Cache-Control private, so a shared cache cannot hand it to a caller without a session.

Search terms take the LIKE wildcards literally, the search accepts only the two filters it reads (strict, bounded lists), and a filter value outside the column's declared values is refused with 400 instead of reaching the database as a 500. The same service also excludes decisions marked not public or restricted.

The unclaimed-workbook read runs under the explicit system context, as the start and claim routes do, instead of on the pooled connection with no user context. Test adapted to the new context call; new tests cover 404 and 503.

An archived incident or hazard is neither listed nor returned by id (the new readCondition), and the statistics, trends and dashboard no longer count it as open, critical or part of a total. Verified later: the dashboard counts exclude archived hazards and the critical-alert count excludes archived incidents; list and item reads carry the archived exclusion on both tables.

batches.family: F04/F12: a row served as analytics comes from a job, a stored object is attached only if nothing else holds it, and a reference profile states only what was measured

items.explanation: Twenty-nine analytics routes over the metric and trend tables keep their read and answer every create with 501, so a steward can no longer insert a row that is then served as computed analytics. A test scans every such route for the factory POST and for the 501 helper.

An upload names a stored object only if no document, and no version of one, in the organization already holds it; an object another record holds answers 409 and inserts nothing. Tests added for both holders.
items.remaining: An unattached object under the organization prefix is still accepted: nothing yet proves it was uploaded by this representative for this matter (an upload-intake record bound to the representative is needed).

items.explanation: X publishing refuses every remote media URL (existing refusal and test); the LinkedIn path, which does fetch a caller-supplied image, now follows no redirect, accepts only an image content type and refuses an image over 8 MB, with tests.

The profile states no default testimonial, no six-hour floor and no 90-day outcomes: a quote appears only when supplied and always as unattested, time saved is null, the case study lists outcomes only when a stored metrics row exists, and the data source is labelled.
The precedent and procedural engines refuse with NOT_IMPLEMENTED for every organization and return no constant profile (existing implementation and test).

The continuity forecast reports no trend and no projection instead of an improving curve from fixed rates, and bases its metrics on eligible interviews, proven against a real SQL engine (existing implementation and test).

batches.family: F06: an audit read serves the record and not the captured values, a recorded position and its audit commit together, and a GET changes nothing

items.explanation: The organization audit-log list names eight columns (who, what, which resource, severity, outcome, time) and no longer serves the captured old and new values, network address, user agent, session and correlation ids, metadata, error text or archive path. The read is still audited in the same transaction.

The position insert and an audit record (purpose, strike or event, never the coordinates) commit in one transaction; a member who has not opted in gets 403, a disabled tracker 503, and any other failure a 500 without internal text. Test mocks extended for the new collaborators; three new route tests.
The investigations path was an alias of the case collection (a create made a case); it answers 501 and the roster-facade ratchet pins it.
The investigation audit path no longer returns the organization audit log under another name; it answers 501.

The two investigation aliases lost their always-true guard along with their delegation. Completed: the intelligence and governance aliases are plain re-exports and the investigations routes answer 501 (verified).
Reading a clause by id writes nothing. Test adapted from countView true to false; the clause view counter is no longer incremented by a read.

batches.family: F05: a list is bounded, a field is bounded, and a filter filters by the values the record can hold

items.explanation: Each of the six pension list reads returns at most 200 rows. Test mock adapted only to expose the added limit call.
items.remaining: There is still no pagination: rows beyond the 200 cap are not reachable through these routes.

items.explanation: The agreement list refuses a page outside 1..10000 or a limit outside 1..100 with 400 instead of passing an unparsed number to the query.
Reading one agreement counts no view, whatever the include flags; the view counter is no longer incremented by a read.
The alert and report lists return at most 500 rows (the failure answer was fixed in B33).

Every contact field has a length bound (name 100, address 254, organization 200, role and inquiry type 100) and the visitor's address is no longer written to the log; tests cover an oversized field and the log content.
The precedent collection refuses an invalid page or a limit above 100 with 400 (existing implementation and tests).

The status filter reaches the query (and its total), and the accepted values are the six the redemption status can hold, including the ones a redemption starts in. Two existing assertions adapted for the added argument; new tests cover a valid and an invalid status.
The transcription response carries no duration: neither bytes nor a guess is reported as a measured audio duration (existing implementation and test).

batches.family: F07: a committee's working record is read by staff and its own members, and a read names only what the caller may see

items.explanation: The five committee read routes (meetings, meeting detail, attendance, action items, documents) require the committee to be the organization's and the reader to be staff or an active member of that committee; any other member gets the not-found answer. Tests cover staff, an active member, an outsider, no identity and another organization's committee.
items.remaining: The committee directory entry itself stays readable by every member (without notes), and the minutes read is steward-level but not checked against membership.

items.explanation: A session read omits the virtual-meeting access code and the session budget and actual cost (existing implementation, pinned by the F07 contract test).
The incident, hazard and inspection item routes block a status or outcome PATCH (existing implementation, pinned by the F07 contract test).
A legacy organization switch needs an active, non-removed membership of an active organization (B21 implementation, pinned by the F07 contract test).
The completions list reads only completed registrations of the caller's organization.
The legacy event item delegates to the canonical calendar route, which applies private and confidential visibility and selects no meeting password or access code.

batches.family: F01/F09/F10: a registry names replacements that exist, a job pages its scan and awaits its writes, and a read honours the record's state and the feature gate

items.explanation: Seven registry rows named replacement routes that do not exist; they now name the real route (current-user, message thread, strike funds) or REMOVED with the reason. A test checks every named replacement against the route tree. A sunset date already past is no longer advertised in a Sunset header, and the body states that it has passed.

The watchdog keyset-pages the claims scan under a page cap, assesses each claim once, awaits the metric writes keyed by organization and hour, and reports a failed metric or alert write as a failed job (existing implementation, existing route and pglite tests).

The session list reads active sessions only, and the message read needs the entitlement, the AI feature flag, the safety check and the rate limit, and refuses an archived or deleted session (existing implementation and test).
Production with no application URL refuses to open a session instead of redirecting a buyer to localhost (existing implementation and test).
items.remaining: A configured Stripe price id can still differ from the amount the application displays; nothing compares them.

batches.family: F05: financial intelligence needs a live financial mandate, and a record a person raises cannot pass for an engine record

items.explanation: The finance analysis and the three pension intelligence routes first require a live finance:view mandate (in the caller own tenant context) and answer 403 without it, before the rate limit, feature gate, entitlement or any read. The finance analysis test mock gained the new collaborator and a refusal test.
items.remaining: The view mandate is not resource-scoped to a plan or member, and the pension projection still reads any member of the plan by id for an officer.

items.explanation: Raising a compliance event is a financial-role act; a manual flag may be info or warning only, can never block an approval, cannot take an engine event code (it is prefixed manual_), and its summary and code are bounded; unknown body fields are refused.

The compliance event list moves from the member floor to the financial roles and is bounded to 500 rows; the payroll and remittance run lists already require the financial roles and a live view mandate.

batches.family: F05: a page request is parsed into bounded integers and an export is bounded, administrative and audited

items.explanation: Limit and offset are parsed to bounded integers (limit 1..100, offset 0..1,000,000), so a non-numeric or negative value is the default rather than NaN or a negative offset; the route reads only the caller own balance and ledger.
items.remaining: The balance and the ledger are still read in two separate statements, so a movement between them can make them disagree.

items.explanation: The export needs the administrator role before any read, is bounded to 5,000 rows, neutralises spreadsheet formula cells, and is audited in the transaction that reads it so a failed audit withholds the file (existing implementation and test).

batches.family: F08: the server fetches a supplied address only if it is a public http(s) address, follows each redirect by hand and reads a bounded document

items.explanation: A shared guard refuses non-http(s) schemes, credentials in the address, localhost and internal names, private, loopback, link-local, metadata and reserved IPv4 and IPv6 literals (including IPv4-mapped forms). The base adapter checks every address before fetching, follows redirects by hand (three at most) re-checking each hop, and refuses a source larger than 10 million characters; every ingestion adapter fetches through it, and a source address is checked when it is saved. B91: the fetch guard now also resolves the host name and refuses a name that resolves to a private, loopback, link-local or reserved address, or does not resolve (assertPublicHttpUrlResolved, used by the base adapter before every fetch and redirect hop); the source update route applies the same public-address rule as registration; the oversized-body refusals are in the adapter tests. Seven adapter test files mock DNS because their fixtures use names that do not exist, and the f08 outbound contract pin reads the resolving guard (disclosed). A name that changes between the lookup and the connection is still the egress policy's to stop.

batches.family: F12: a failure is answered as a failure without internal text, and a query is validated

items.explanation: A failed indexing now returns a result flagged failed with the fixed text "Indexing failed" (the error stays in the audit record), and the index route answers it 500 instead of 200 carrying the error. Two existing indexer assertions adapted: they required the raw error text ("audit down", "embed boom") in the reason, which is the defect; they now require the fixed text and the absence of the error text.

The query is validated (nodeId bounded text, analysisType one of four values, unknown parameters refused), an unknown node answers 404 instead of a thrown 500. Verified and completed: an unknown node is a 404, the query is a strict schema, and each analysis type, node view included, returns only its own section.

batches.family: F05: a numeric query parameter is parsed into a bounded integer, and a telemetry body is bounded

items.explanation: The telemetry body is bounded to 2 KB while it is streamed (not only by Content-Length), the payload is reduced to an allow-list of canonical event, tab and static route, and the client attests to no timestamp or workspace name (existing implementation and tests). Verified in source: the route has its own per-user rate limit (120 a minute, refusing when the limiter is unavailable) and logs only the allow-listed event, tab and static route with a server-set timestamp.

The comment must be text of at most 2000 characters (trimmed; an empty one is stored as none), a body that is not a JSON object is refused, and the administrator summary no longer returns the author user id of recent feedback. New route test covers each.

The pilot events and feedback writes bound their free-form fields (session id 200 characters, metadata a plain object of at most 4 KB, comment 2000 characters) and refuse a body that is not a JSON object; tests added for each bound. Completed: the four POST handlers parse their body through length-bounded schemas (lib/pilot/write-payloads.ts; an absent body is the empty object, a malformed, mistyped, oversized or non-object body is a 400 or 413, unknown keys are dropped), so no caller text reaches the jsonb column unbounded.

batches.family: F05: signature records disclose only what the viewer is entitled to and are bounded; a search term is literal and bounded

items.explanation: The void PATCH now applies its schema: a strict body with the literal action void and a trimmed reason of 1 to 1000 characters. A body that does not match is a 400 and nothing is stored. Contract test added.
Both queries of the caller own document list (sent and to-sign) are limited to 200 rows, newest first, and the to-sign side returns only the caller own signer row. Contract test pins both limits.
items.remaining: No cursor or offset parameter yet; the newest 200 are returned.

items.explanation: The status, the audit trail and the audit report keep every signer network address, user agent and geolocation for the sender only. A signer sees those fields only on the rows that describe themselves. Unit tests cover sender, signer and audit rows. The audit route test mock gained getDocumentSender (disclosed adaptation).
items.remaining: Signer e-mail addresses are still visible to every signer, and the report actor and signer rows carry no user id, so a signer own network data is also withheld from the report.

items.explanation: The audit report no longer reads as certified evidence: it carries an integrity block stating the trail is unsealed, not hash-chained and not tamper-evident.
items.remaining: No hash chain, file-hash recomputation at signing, or sealing is implemented, and the signer address still comes from a client-supplied forwarded header.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: recordSignature refuses an expired request and enforces sequential signing order, each with a test.
items.remaining: The requireAuthentication option is still stored and not enforced, and nothing sets the expired status for an internal document.

items.explanation: The search term is trimmed, bounded to 100 characters (400 beyond), and its LIKE wildcards are taken literally. Results are ordered by name then id and paged by limit (at most 50) and offset. The test mock chain was adapted to the ordered, paged query (disclosed), and a new test covers escaping, bounds and offset.
Existing implementation, verified: a malformed target id is a 400 before any database predicate is built, with an existing test that no query or audit happens.
items.remaining: The route still offers no edit, rename or delete of a target.

batches.family: F03/F05: the shared clause library validates what it stores, reserves public publishing to an officer, and writes only rows it owns

items.explanation: Clause create, update and sharing bodies pass a zod schema before anything is stored: text, titles and names are bounded, dates are real calendar days, province is a 2-letter code, ids are ids, sharing levels are the four known ones, grants are at most 200 ids, and unknown fields are dropped. A malformed body is a 400. Existing route tests were adapted: organization and agreement fixtures that were not ids became ids, and handler calls that publish publicly carry an officer role (disclosed). Verified later: create, update and share parse their body with parseClauseBody and the tag routes with parseClauseTagBody, so no malformed field reaches the database.

Setting a clause to public sharing on create, update or the share route now requires an officer role; a steward, a member or an unresolved role is refused with 403 before any read or write. Narrower scopes stay with the owning steward and keep their federation and congress eligibility checks. Verified later: create, update and share all call assertMayPublish, so public sharing needs an officer role on every path.

A cited originalClauseId must be a clause of a collective agreement of the caller own organization (joined through the agreement); a missing or foreign one is a 404 and nothing is inserted. The id must also be well-formed.

A comparison no longer increments comparisonCount on rows another organization owns: it is a read of those rows and writes only the usage counter of the caller own clauses. The audit stays with the comparing organization.

batches.family: F12: an ICRA assessment exists only with server-stamped consent and is scored only from the required answers

items.explanation: The one-shot submit builds the stored consent on the server from the three acknowledgements (time and doctrine version stamped here; client time, version and extra keys dropped), accepts only the en-CA and fr-CA locales, reads the body as text under a 64 KB cap (413 beyond), and refuses organization-context keys that are not short lower-case identifiers or exceed 40. Unit and source-contract tests added; existing route tests still pass.

The stepwise flow requires all three acknowledgements to start (400 otherwise, consent stamped by the server), the answer route refuses to store anything for an assessment with no recorded consent (409), and so does the stepwise submit. No application caller of these routes existed. Existing tests were adapted: assessment fixtures now carry a recorded consent, the start 500 test sends consent, and the submit tests mock the coverage helper (disclosed); new tests cover the refusals.

The stepwise submit scores nothing unless every question the routing engine requires for an unclassified organization has an answer (400 with the missing count otherwise), using the same routed-submission validator as the live flow. Proven against the real question bank: one answer is refused, a full set is accepted.

batches.family: F12: cognition and knowledge-transfer results do not present absence, defaults or literals as measurement

items.explanation: The documentation strategy is selected when the documentation score is low (under 65) or unmeasured (missing or not finite), and not for any high score. The expression that parsed as score ?? (0 < 65) is gone. Source-contract test added.
The precedence defect in the documentation rule is corrected (same fix as the companion defect).
items.remaining: The projected resilience, governance and dependency gains of each strategy are still literal numbers from a per-strategy table.

items.explanation: With fewer than two entries and sessions the profiler now returns a new insufficient_data type with no characteristics and an identity statement that says so, instead of Resilience-Fragile. The existing no-history test pinned the old label and was changed to assert the new behaviour (disclosed).

Every derived analysis that read all published exit interviews now reads at most 500, newest as the database returns them, through one shared constant, so the work and the model prompt no longer grow without bound. Six test mocks gained a limit step on the query chain (disclosed; behaviour unchanged). Verified later: the topic graph, propagation map, resilience index and succession analyzer each read at most INTERVIEW_READ_LIMIT (500) published interviews, which also bounds the succession prompt and the tag pairs.

A narrative whose envelope carries no evidence now says that no institutional evidence is attached and that the result is guidance, not a finding, instead of "Derived from 0 institutional evidence items".
items.remaining: The headline is still the first sentence of fixed interpretation guidance and the engines still emit no evidence, reasoning or implications.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the resilience index refuses an organization with no dependency data with a conflict instead of computing NaN scores, so no strong status or brief is derived from it; an existing test covers both the empty and the interviews-without-nodes cases.

batches.family: F05/F12: searches match literally and list only active organizations; free-form JSON from callers is bounded and cannot overwrite audited fields

items.explanation: The organization search always excludes the platform organization type and any organization whose status is not active (a missing status counts as active), with or without a term, matches the term literally (percent and underscore escaped), and orders by name then id. The real-SQL pglite test for the search still passes, and a source-contract test pins the predicates.

The onboarding event payload bounds targetUserId (255) and role (64), limits metadata to 20 keys of short scalar values, and stores caller metadata before targetUserId and role so it can never replace the values the audit row records.
items.remaining: The event is still a caller-asserted milestone (tracked by the companion defect).

items.explanation: The anonymous pilot application bounds responses to 16 KB, 60 keys and 4 levels of nesting, and keeps only a finite numeric or short string assessment score instead of a passthrough object. Unit tests cover each bound. Verified later: responses go through boundedJsonRecord (16 KB, 60 keys, depth 4) and an assessment keeps only its score.

batches.family: F06: regulatory records and integration sync history are not erased by the generic delete

items.explanation: New crud-factory option retainOnDelete: DELETE answers 409 before any lookup or write, so the row is kept. Applied to the anti-scab violation and joint health-and-safety committee item routes, the two tables the defect names. A contract test pins that the refusal comes before any audited write or tx.delete.
The right-of-refusal item route declares retainOnDelete, so the refusal record and any reprisal complaint are never removed through the generic delete (409).
items.remaining: No retention rule is named by a source, so the record is retained rather than archived; a governed withdrawal action is still to be defined.

items.explanation: Deleting an integration first confirms it belongs to the organization (404 otherwise), then refuses with 409 when any synchronization history exists, so the cascade can never erase it; the integration is disabled instead. The existing extensions test was adapted to the new query sequence and gained the history case (disclosed).

batches.family: F05/F03: the social export is a bounded staff read with safe cells; records are looked up inside the caller organization

items.explanation: The social analytics export no longer executes on DELETE: that verb returns 405, while GET ?export=true is separately steward-gated. The export rejects invalid format/date windows and refuses oversized results rather than silently truncating them; CSV remains formula-neutralized and account follower columns now map correctly. A mandatory tenant-bound audit is persisted before any CSV/JSON response; audit failures return 503 without exporting data. Both response types prohibit caching. Source and regression tests are committed but executable and runtime qualification are pending.
items.remaining: Exact-HEAD focused and full Vitest/contract, native PostgreSQL 15/16 with real RLS and audit storage, HTTP/browser/staging acceptance, and institutional decision on export audience remain outstanding. Campaign export still uses bounded per-campaign queries and needs scalable server-side aggregation; no production acceptance claimed.

items.explanation: The post delete and the campaign analytics lookups name the caller organization inside the query (the post through an inner join to its account), so another organization row is simply not found (404) and the 403-versus-404 existence oracle is gone. The campaign routes already did this. The post delete test mock gained the inner join and now expects 404 for a foreign post (disclosed).

batches.family: F08: stored credentials and access configuration fail closed

items.explanation: The SSO provider create now accepts only saml or oidc, bounds every text field, requires https URLs without credentials for the SSO URL and issuer, requires the fields of the type when the provider is to be enabled, and creates a provider disabled and without auto-provisioning unless the administrator asks otherwise. The existing route tests pass unchanged; new unit tests cover each rule.
items.remaining: No unique index on organization, entity id or issuer, no proof the organization owns the identity domain, and requireGroups still cannot be set.

items.explanation: A provider token is never stored without an encryption key (development included; plaintext only under the test runner), and a stored value with no encryption prefix is refused unless CALENDAR_TOKEN_ALLOW_LEGACY_PLAINTEXT is set for a flagged migration window. New unit tests cover round trip, missing key in development and production, and the legacy flag.
items.remaining: Existing plaintext rows need a one-time re-encryption or re-authorization; none is performed here.

items.explanation: The entitlement list now names only the feature keys that the server-side checkModuleEntitlement allows (not expired, backing contract active) and is limited to 200 rows. Contract test pins the check.

batches.family: F03: an id taken from a body must name a row of the caller organization

items.explanation: The training session create checks that the course is the organization own (shared reference helper, 404 otherwise) and accepts only an allow-list of descriptive fields: registration, waitlist, attendance, completion, rating, evaluation, cost, status and cancellation figures are no longer body-writable. Contract test pins the allow-list and the check.

Logging an employer communication checks employerId, grievanceId, recipientContactId and templateId against the caller organization before any write (404, nothing written or audited), and the list is limited to 200. The existing route test mock gained the limit step and a new test covers a foreign grievance (disclosed).

batches.family: F12: routes that record a send or advertise an operation they do not perform answer 501; communications history is retained

items.explanation: The SMS message, campaign and conversation collections keep their officer-floor read, and their POST (which inserted rows carrying status, provider id, price and delivery times for messages never sent) now answers 501 and writes nothing. Contract test pins the read and the refusal.

The conversation read path no longer lists every message of the organization or inserts a message row: both methods answer 501 at the officer floor. The F07 read-authority contract test listed this path among the CRUD floors and was adjusted to drop it (disclosed); the new test pins the 501.
Both message-template item routes declare retainOnDelete: DELETE answers 409 and the template (and the campaign links it keeps) survives.
items.remaining: No archive or withdrawal action exists yet, so a template can no longer be removed through the API.

items.remaining: No archive action exists yet.

items.explanation: A job id that is not a campaign job, or a campaign of another organization, is answered 404 instead of a fabricated processing status with a start time of now; the failed-recipient list names a recipient id, not an e-mail address.
Existing implementation, verified by a new source-contract test: both filing paths answer 501 and neither is the generic campaign CRUD any more.

The generation endpoint already refuses unsupported work with 501. The client now checks HTTP success, application/pdf content type, PDF magic bytes, and a 20 MB safety ceiling before creating a downloadable file. A 501 or JSON success-looking response produces an accessible visible error instead of a mislabeled PDF. Template selection now fills the selected template, and the federal information link no longer falsely advertises electronic filing. Focused regression tests are committed but not executed on this HEAD.
items.remaining: A real jurisdiction-specific PDF generator, template authority/legal review, PDF content validation, and exact-HEAD unit, native PostgreSQL, HTTP/browser and staging acceptance remain outstanding; the client explicitly preserves entered values on refusal.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the bookings path answers 501 for GET and POST, reads and writes no room or booking row.
items.remaining: The room_bookings table is not migrated; the booking rules in lib/services/room-booking-rules.ts are not wired in.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the carbon dashboard no longer reads an organization id from the query string and no longer returns figures; it answers 501.

Existing implementation, verified: the response create verifies the survey belongs to the caller organization, is active and open, and strips respondent identity for an anonymous survey; the list is a count-only steward read of the path survey. Verified in source: POST binds the survey to the path (a body value may not change it), checks the survey belongs to the organization and is open, and GET returns counts for the path survey only.

batches.family: F12: referenced ids belong to the right parent, and a figure with nothing to measure is unknown rather than 0 or 100

items.remaining: The direction is inferred from threshold order because no direction column exists; a column is the proper fix. The current value is still the latest row of the metric type.

The filings collection sets staffReadsAll, so the member-id owner scope applies only below the steward floor and a steward reads the organization filings, as the item routes already allow.

Deadline adherence and documentation rate are null, not 100, when there is nothing to measure, and the card shows a dash in a neutral colour. The empty-input service test pinned the 100 and was changed to expect null (disclosed).
items.remaining: No code inserts compliance alerts, and the grievance aggregates still stop at the first 5000 rows.

items.explanation: The inspection findings list reports a missing score as null (shown as a dash) instead of 0%. The statistics and dashboard routes already reported unmeasured values as null (existing implementation, existing tests pass).
Adding a primary contact demotes the employer previous primary contact in the same transaction, so at most one is primary per create.
items.remaining: No unique index enforces it, so two concurrent creates could still both be primary.

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified by a new test: neither collection declares an owner column the table lacks, so no declared-but-unapplied owner condition remains.
Existing implementation, verified by a new test: event create checks the calendar belongs to the caller organization and is not another member personal calendar (404).
items.remaining: The event update route does not re-check a changed calendarId.

batches.family: F12: publication needs a second person, and registration follows the session window and capacity

items.explanation: Moving an item from review to published is refused for the person who last changed it (who moved it to review), and republishing no longer rewrites the first publication time (coalesce). Existing status route tests pass.
items.remaining: The row records only its last editor, not a separate submitter; a submitted_by column is the proper fix.

items.explanation: Registration is refused (409) for a session that is not scheduled, outside its registration window, or at its maximum enrollment (counted from registered rows). The session-belongs-to-course and duplicate checks already existed. The route test mock gained the count helper and new cases for closed, not-yet-open, cancelled and full sessions (disclosed).
