batches.family: Schema closure: the columns and indexes that let earlier partial fixes record the real fact instead of approximating it

items.explanation: Migration 0038 adds kpi_configurations.direction (higher_is_better or lower_is_better, null for rows that predate it). A target can be created with a direction, and the summary lets a stored direction decide; only a target with none keeps the threshold-order inference. Proven on PGlite (check constraint) and by unit tests.

Migration 0038 adds a partial unique index so an employer has at most one active primary contact; it refuses to apply over an employer that already has two. The create keeps its in-transaction demotion and answers a lost race with 409. Proven on PGlite, including the refusal over existing duplicates.

Migration 0038 adds committee_meetings.minutes_recorded_by and a check that the approver is not the recorder. Recording the minutes stores the recorder and approval refuses that person (403); a meeting recorded before the column existed falls back to its last editor.

Migration 0038 adds exit_interviews.submitted_by and a check that the reviewer is not the submitter. Submitting stores the submitter and review refuses that person (403), with the last-editor fallback only for earlier rows. Existing review tests pass.

Migration 0038 adds cms_pages.submitted_by. Moving an item to review records who did it, and publication is refused for that person, with the last-editor fallback only for earlier rows. Existing status tests pass.

No schema change was needed: the tables already carry is_active. The shared CRUD factory gains archiveColumn, so DELETE archives the template (is_active false, audited) instead of removing it, and the collections list active templates only. The B53 retain-on-delete pin was replaced by an archive pin (disclosed).

DELETE of a distribution list now archives it (is_active false), so the cascade that erased the subscribed, unsubscribed and unsubscribe-reason trail can no longer fire through the API; the collection lists active lists only.

Migration 0038 adds unique partial indexes (organization and SAML entity id; organization, OIDC issuer and client id), refusing to apply over duplicates; a duplicate create answers 409. The create now accepts requireGroups (at most 50 short names). Proven on PGlite.
items.remaining: No proof that the organization owns the identity domain: that needs a DNS or e-mail verification process with the identity provider, which a schema cannot supply.

batches.family: Database enforcement: constraints, triggers and columns that settle what application checks could only attempt

items.explanation: Migration 0040 adds new_engine to employer_execution_replay_mode, so an engine-change replay is stored as new_engine and not as a faithful exact re-run. Proven on PGlite; the requested mode still travels with the diff for idempotency.

Migration 0040 adds a unique index (organization, member, session) that refuses to apply over existing duplicates, and a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that locks the session row and refuses a registration beyond max_enrollment (SQLSTATE 23514); a cancelled place frees a seat and a re-save of a registered row is not recounted. The CRUD factory gains mapCreateError so a lost race answers 409 (full, or already registered). Proven on PGlite.
Migration 0040 adds ml_predictions.subject_id. The case is verified against the organization (B08) and is now stored on the prediction row, and the audit entry and feedback carry it.

Migration 0040 adds ml_predictions.model_version, written by the prediction route. Feedback now defaults to the version the prediction recorded and refuses (409) a different one, so the version binding no longer depends on a column that was missing. The route test zod mock gained optional() on min() (disclosed).

The durable sent marker needed no new table: the warning is also the member's in-app notice, recorded in in_app_notifications under data.dedupeKey (unique per organization and member, migration 20261103) before the mail leaves; a second run, retry or overlap mails nothing more, and a failed send releases the record so the next run tries again. Proved on PostgreSQL (PGlite) for repeat, retry-after-failure and per-tier behaviour. The mocked notification-service test now mocks the marker (disclosed).
items.remaining: Nothing in the product sets an expiry or writes an expire entry yet, so the task still has nothing to warn about until an expiry policy is decided and implemented.

batches.family: Room booking: the booking store, its tenant isolation and the route that enforces the room's own rules

The f12-b53 contract pin that listed this route as 501 was removed (disclosed).

batches.family: F05 input validation and bounds: typed bodies, bounded pages and limited anonymous reads

items.explanation: Existing implementation, verified: the four administrator-only CLC analytics routes answer Cache-Control private, no-store; pinned by a test that also refuses any public value.

The meeting list takes a bounded limit (1..200, default 50) and offset (0..1,000,000) and the intelligence list a bounded limit (1..100, default 20) through listPage; a non-numeric or negative value is the default and NaN never reaches the query.

Both content lists take a bounded limit (1..200; training default 200, templates default 50) and offset through listPage, ordered with the id as a tie-break so a page is stable; a negative or non-numeric limit is the default instead of a SQL error.

The resume, profile and PDF report reads now pass through guardPublicIntake with the capability bucket before any lookup or render; a limited caller gets 429 (503 when the limiter is unavailable in production). The report route test mocks the guard and gained a test that a limited caller triggers no lookup and no render (disclosed).

The body is parsed as JSON (400 otherwise) and validated: a trimmed bounded name and description, a type from strike_line, union_hall and safety_zone, numeric coordinates in range, a positive radius of at most 10 km; strikeId is refused because no strike register exists to prove it belongs to the organization. The invoice replay, the last non-atomic item, reads the invoice and its lineage and writes its access record with persistAtomicAudit in one tenant transaction, before anything is returned: if the record cannot be written the lineage is not released, and a replay of an invoice that is not found writes no record. With invoice generation and trial expiry already atomic, the three operations the defect names are now all atomic; the route manifest classifies the route ATOMIC from its own source.

The closure of a lapsed designation during a fresh grant returns the closed rows and writes a triage.designation.expire audit record for each, in the same transaction, attributed to system:expiry (kept in the metadata, as persistAtomicAudit does for system actors) with the administrator who triggered the closure.

The export writes a workbook.export audit record (authority kind, size) through the claimed-workbook audit helper before the PDF is returned, and fails closed when the record cannot be written. The loader no longer selects the display name of every holder, which the template never printed. The export route test was extended (disclosed): it mocks the audit helper and adds the audit, audit-failure and ineligible-tier cases.

The access record carries the caller and organization from the handler context and is awaited; a failure to record is logged and the answer stays 410. The catch-all test was extended (disclosed): it supplies the identity, asserts it, mocks the logger and adds the failed-record case.

Verified in source: the employer risk calculation and the insight report no longer insert employer_risk_scores or ai_insight_reports on a GET (the comment records that persistence needs a separately authorized, audited command); the invocation is audited.

batches.family: Social campaign figures, publish handling and token refresh

items.explanation: One helper computes the campaign totals, the per-platform figures (from the count fields the query selects, not impressions/engagement/likes names it does not return), the average engagement rate (absent when no post has one) and the progress toward the goals the campaign set (impressions, engagement rate; conversions have no actual because none is collected). The clicks total is absent, not zero; both reads add the organization predicate on posts; the responses carry figures_recorded so default zeros are not presented as measured performance.

A platform failure is returned as a fixed message (this application's own refusals keep their text; the platform's text is logged, not returned); a failure to save the row after the platform accepted the post is reported as published and unrecorded (recorded: false) and logged, not as a failed publish; when no platform accepted the post the audited operation throws, so its outcome record says failed. Two tests were adapted and three added (disclosed): the route test mock gained the error class, the service test gained the three cases.
items.remaining: The intent and outcome records are still written around the external call and are not committed with a data row: an external effect cannot be made atomic with a database row, and a post scheduled or published before the row is saved can still exist without it if the process dies in between.

items.explanation: Only the platform refusing the refresh marks a connected (active) account expired, with an audit record that says whether it did; a storage or audit failure after a successful refresh marks nothing. A suspended or disconnected account is refused with 409 rather than reactivated, and a successful refresh sets an expired account active and keeps any other state. Two tests were added (disclosed).

batches.family: CBA review visibility, benchmark and comparison honesty, cognition health scope, derived case metrics, metrics organization binding

items.explanation: A member reads approved extractions only (list, export, and the agreement with its wage adjustments and clauses; an unapproved agreement answers 404 so its existence is not disclosed); a steward or above, the reviewers, may name any review status to read the queue.
The snapshot history no longer returns the computedBy user id: the snapshots belong to the platform-wide dataset, so who saved one is platform information and is not shown to a tenant reader.

The comparison no longer returns three fixed recommendation sentences: differences, best practices and recommendations stay empty and the result states analysis grouped_by_type_only, since no wording is compared.

An organization officer receives the status and check time only; the registry, ontology and contract versions and the engine counts per domain are returned to a platform administrator. The route test was extended (disclosed): it mocks the platform-administrator check and asserts the reduced payload.

The case counts (opened and closed in the window, open now) are read from the claims table of the organization under its tenant context at the steward floor; overdue cases and SLA compliance are returned as null because a claim records no deadline or status-change time. The weekly summary labels its telemetry count caseCreatedEvents.

The metrics routes pass the organization they authorized to the actions, which refuse the call when their own verified resolution differs, so a user with several memberships cannot write to an organization other than the one the role check was made in.
Verified in source: the synthesis POST validates every named committee and then answers 501 without gathering minutes or storing a snapshot.

batches.family: Social scheduling and campaign link, graph query inputs, health-safety statistics

items.explanation: A schedule is passed on only to Facebook, whose API schedules; for Instagram, X and LinkedIn the platform entry is refused ("not published") instead of publishing at once under a row that says scheduled. Hashtags are written into the post text that is sent (and an X post over 280 characters with them is refused); mentions, which no platform integration sends, are refused with 400. The scheduled-carousel service test, which pinned an immediate LinkedIn publish of a scheduled post, was changed to Facebook and its assertion to the scheduled publish time (disclosed); four cases were added.

The post route verifies campaign_id belongs to the organization (404 otherwise), passes it on, and the service stores it as the post campaignId, so campaign metrics and the campaign delete guard see the post.

The request schema is strict: category, roleFilter and depthLimit, which the reasoner never read, are refused (400); minimumRiskLevel is accepted only for isolated_knowledge, the one query that applies it; explanationLevel is optional and the response states one level and the filters actually applied.

batches.family: Interview document location, cascade wording, per-capita job, education reminder cap, precedent reads

items.explanation: A document location must be https on an exact approved host (UE_DOCUMENT_STORAGE_HOSTS, default the shared storage account; a subdomain is another party's host and is refused), carry no credentials, query string or fragment (so a signed-access token is never stored), and have the organization id as a path segment so one organization cannot register another's object; localhost is accepted outside production only. The attach test body was moved to a path inside the organization area and four refusal cases were added (disclosed). The storage path convention (organization id as a segment) is a rule this change introduces: no uploader in the repository produces these URLs, so the client of the presigned-URL flow must follow it. B86: the producer of the required location now exists. POST /api/exit-interviews/[id]/documents/upload (steward or owner, entitlement-gated) scans the file for malware before storing anything, stores it at interviews/<organizationId>/<interviewId>/<random>-<name> in the approved storage account, registers the unsigned object location with an atomic audit record, and removes the stored object if the record cannot be written.

regulatoryRisks lists only the areas that depend on a compliance node, worded as a dependency ("Depends on a compliance node: X"), with regulatoryAssessment dependency_only_no_regulation_assessed; the three fixed recommendation sentences are gone (the list is empty). The analyzer test was rewritten for this (disclosed).

The monthly per-capita route no longer calculates or writes anything: it answers 501 to an administrator (the affiliate remittance capability is NOT_IMPLEMENTED), and its schedule entry is removed so no monthly run fails for it. The calculator service and its tests are untouched.
Each reminder kind is capped at 300 recipients per run, the remainder is reported as truncated in the job details and logged, so the run no longer grows with the member count past the job timeout.

Verified in source: every library read (by id, case number, list, search, issue type, related, statistics, most cited) filters isPublic and empty access restrictions in SQL, and the list, issue-type, most-cited and search routes answer an explicit public projection without the full text, grievor, remedy or provenance columns.

batches.family: Cognition reads follow the case authority

items.explanation: The risk score is computed only for a case the authority kernel lets the caller read (case:read_internal, the decision the case routes use); any other case answers 404. The precedent search requires the searched case to be readable, validates the case ids (at most 50 candidates) and compares only candidates the caller may read, so it never returns the title of a case the steward does not hold.

The workload route, which returns each steward's burnout signal, utilization and recommended reassignments, is at the officer floor instead of the steward floor, so a steward no longer reads a colleague's burnout signal.

batches.family: Small validation and verification items

items.explanation: Resolving or writing off an exception now requires a stated reason of at least 10 characters after trimming (an empty string was accepted), on top of the live financial mandate and the admin floor the route already required.
items.remaining: A second approver and any ledger effect of a write-off are not implemented: they are finance workflow decisions that sit under the finance freeze.

batches.family: Owner decisions applied: organization types, calendar revocation, bot challenge

items.explanation: The create handler stores description, province, charter number and affiliation date in their columns. The hierarchy admin selector now offers the canonical types (platform, congress, federation, union, local, region, district) in English and French instead of the legacy labels the handler refused, and create and update decide success from the HTTP status (the handler never returned a success field) and show the refusal.

A member disconnects their own calendar (member floor, own connection only). The provider is asked to revoke the grant first (Google: the token revocation endpoint with a 5 second bound; Microsoft has no per-token revocation, so it reports not_supported rather than ending every session of the person), the local credentials are then deleted whatever the provider answered, and the audit row and the response say what happened (providerRevocation, providerRevocationVerified). The owner-scoping delete test was rewritten for the two-step flow and two cases were added (disclosed).

The contact route asks for a Cloudflare Turnstile token (guardPublicIntake challenge: true: x-turnstile-token header or the body turnstileToken, stripped before the route sees the body). Production fails closed: no configured secret answers 503 and an unreachable verifier is a refusal; outside production an unconfigured challenge is open. The contact form renders the widget when a site key is configured and sends the token. The address the limit keys on was already the trusted-hop address (earlier batch).

The ICRA start and checkout and the workbook start and checkout routes ask for the same Turnstile token and fail closed in production; ICRA submit, which already verified a token, now refuses (503) in production when no secret is configured instead of treating the challenge as satisfied. The report checkout component renders the widget and sends the token. The workbook start page writes through a server component, not this route, and is unchanged.

batches.family: Platform reads, communications tracking and unsubscribe, signature service

items.explanation: Verified on source in B87: the three platform metric routes are at the system_admin floor (not the organization administrator floor) and read no table: each answers 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED until a platform-data mandate and source reconciliation exist, so no revenue or churn aggregate reaches any administrator.

B87: the precedent is created as a draft (not public, access restriction pending_review), the audit row names the supplying organization, and the row itself now records its source as typed:<organizationId>:<userId> in imported_from, since the shared table has no organization column. A typed decision is now owned by the supplying organization (source_organization_id), is created not public with access_restrictions pending_review, and keeps its typed provenance; the row-security policy of cache 0041 means no other organization can change or delete it.
items.remaining: There is still no review, redaction or consent step that moves a decision from pending_review to shared.

items.explanation: Verified on source in B87: the legacy branch is gone from the organizations route; the list is bounded by the caller identity scope and no environment list of platform user ids is read there.

A link without a campaign now revokes in every organization that holds a preference row or a list subscription for the recipient, in the same transaction and through the same helper as a campaign link: preference, list subscriptions and one revoked consent record per organization, each attributed to its organization. The reason text is bounded at 200 characters. The route tests were extended and the b55 pin was adapted to the helper (disclosed). An outbound campaign sender now issues a signed campaign-scoped unsubscribe capability, while explicit all-organization tokens remain separately signed. Missing signing keys refuse sends. Real mail-provider issuance and independent policy approval remain unproven.
items.remaining: Exact-HEAD executable, native and HTTP/browser qualification; provider delivery headers and one-click interoperability; global opt-out institutional semantics.

items.explanation: The click route now matches the open route: one system-context transaction, a conditional UPDATE that elects a single winner for the first click, PostgreSQL jsonb increments (clicked, and opened only when no open was recorded) so concurrent events keep their counts, and an atomic audit record; a failed transaction counts nothing and the verified redirect still happens. The click tests were adapted to the transaction and two cases were added (disclosed).

twilioPhoneNumber is already a protected key that an organization administrator cannot write (earlier batch). B87: the inbound lookup reads two rows and refuses to attribute a message when the number is held by more than one organization, so an ambiguous number can no longer place a member text in the wrong tenant.
The status read no longer calls the provider or writes a row. A sender refreshes explicitly with POST /api/signatures/documents/[id], which runs the existing conditional, audited syncDocumentStatus.

The signer list is validated against active organization members before anything leaves the platform (earlier batch). B87: when the transaction that records the document fails, the provider envelope is voided and the stored file is deleted (best effort, both attempted), and the original failure is reported.

A signer user id must now be an active member of the sending organization when the request is created, so a user of another organization cannot be named as a signer, and the status and audit views are projected per viewer.
items.remaining: verifyDocumentAccess, getDocumentStatus and the audit reads still look the document up by id through the shared handle with no tenant context; they need an organization-bound read path.

batches.family: Audit records: onboarding reads, social connection, integration sync

items.explanation: The three onboarding reads no longer emit to an in-process bus with no subscriber. Each awaits recordOnboardingRead, a canonical audit row (onboarding.federation_discovery, onboarding.peer_benchmarks, onboarding.clause_suggestions) in the acting organization, before the result is returned, and a failed record fails the request. Federation discovery now also requires an organization context. The three route tests were adapted from the bus assertion to the audit writer (disclosed).

No sync engine or adapter performs a dry run, so the route schema accepts dryRun only as false: a request for a dry run is refused with a validation error instead of running a real sync that the audit row calls a dry run.

Listing and initiating a connection now write canonical audit rows (social_account.list, social_account.connect_initiated) and completing one writes social_account.connected in the same transaction as the credential upsert, so a connection with no record is not kept. The log-line helper, which dropped the action, organization and platform, is no longer used by either route. The list test asserts the audit row (disclosed), and the social_accounts importer census gained the review route that earlier batch B85 added.
The completion audit is now an atomic row committed with the credential upsert (social_account.connected).
items.remaining: The callback is still a GET that clears its state cookies before validating the request, so a forged request can clear a pending connection; changing the verb or the cookie order needs a coordinated change with the provider redirect registration.

batches.family: Stored report contract, cross-organization read authority, AI data class, verified signer and list fixes

items.explanation: The execute route allowlists moved into lib/reports/report-config-validation.ts and the report definition create (beforeCreate) and update (beforeUpdate) now apply them at save time through validateStoredReportConfig: an object of at most 32 KB and depth 6, a registry data source, registry field ids, the executor operator vocabulary, bounded lists, and a join only to a table of the reporting registry; a refused definition answers 400 with the reason instead of being stored as a success. The s19 pin was adapted to read the shared validator (disclosed).

The read no longer depends on whatever the connection role happens to see: it runs under the system role on purpose (the manifest now declares SELECT for the system role on analytics_metrics and the catalog contract was regenerated), returns aggregates only as before, requires an active organization for the caller, and records analytics.cross_org.read in the same transaction as the read. The route test was adapted to the system transaction and a no-organization case was added (disclosed). The platform_lead role-title floor remains the gate, as for the platform statistics read; a platform-staff mandate does not exist yet.

A mapping exists (toGatewayDataClass: confidential and member data to sensitive; restricted, pension_financial and grievance_legal to regulated) and the finance, pension, employer risk, grievance triage, steward copilot and clause reasoning services use it. B87/B89: the three precedent-matching calls that send claim facts (keyword extraction, applicability, strength analysis) now declare regulated instead of internal.
items.remaining: Several other services (auto classification, clause extraction, vector search, copilot, mamba, chatbot, knowledge-transfer) still declare internal literals; each needs a per-surface decision of the class its inputs carry.

items.explanation: Verified on source in B89: the repository list is bounded (listPage, default 50, at most 100 candidate rows with an offset on candidate rows), the case filter is applied in SQL, and the filters are length-checked, so the cost no longer grows with the size of the document store.

Verified on source in B89: the signers list is parsed with a strict schema; a platform signer must be an active member of the sending organization and is stored under that member record name and e-mail address (what the sender typed is discarded); a document held by an external provider is refused for local signing, so it cannot be completed without the provider.

batches.family: Lifecycle routes (health-safety close, SSO provider) and minimum cohort for satisfaction figures

items.explanation: The generic PATCH may not set a status or date, so there was no route that did. POST /api/health-safety/incidents/[id]/close (administrator) moves a reported or investigating incident to closed and stamps the closed and investigation-completed dates, and POST /api/health-safety/hazards/[id]/transition (resolve or close) moves an open hazard on and stamps the resolution date, and the closed date on close. The dates come from the database clock, the change is conditional on the prior status, and the transition is audited in the same transaction. The statistics routes already compute the resolution time from these dates and from no other.
items.remaining: The incident statistics still count a status of resolved that the incident schema does not define; that counter is always zero.

items.explanation: B90: a representative with fewer than five completed responses is returned without any figure (suppressed: true, all averages zero) and is listed after the ranked ones, so a steward who knows which claim the representative handled can no longer read one response back as an average. Platform 0050 makes the promise true in the database: a completed anonymous response is held without member_id and claim_id, without sent_at and metadata, and with its dates coarsened to the month; a CHECK refuses an anonymous completed row that still carries a member or a claim; existing anonymous rows are scrubbed (irreversibly, on purpose). satisfaction_survey_responded keeps only that this member answered this claim, so the survey is not sent again (the service answers 409), and the application roles hold SELECT only on it. The trigger avoids ON CONFLICT, which needs a SELECT policy the table owner does not have under forced row security, and the scrub and the rollback check lift and restore the force. Proven on native PostgreSQL 15 and 16.
items.remaining: Free-text feedback is the respondent's own words and is not altered; it can still name someone.

items.explanation: PATCH /api/enterprise/sso/providers/[id] (administrator) changes, enables, disables or rotates the client secret of one provider of the organization, and DELETE removes it. Unknown fields are refused, a role mapping may only assign roles a tenant administrator can already assign, the merged configuration must be complete for its type to be enabled, a rotated secret is encrypted with the same service as at creation, and every change is audited in the same transaction with the names of the fields and never a credential value. The manifest grants the tenant runtime UPDATE and DELETE on sso_providers (the manifest-driven generator issues the grants, so there is no hand-written migration) and the catalog contract was regenerated; the grants are unqualified until run on native PostgreSQL.

batches.family: Provider token sealing, resolved outbound fetch guard, verified analytics suppression

items.explanation: Provider access and refresh tokens are sealed with the Key-Vault-backed secret service (enc:v1: marker) when the OAuth callback stores them and whenever a refresh rewrites them, and opened only at the point a provider client is built. A token written before sealing existed has no marker, is used as it is, and becomes sealed the next time it is rewritten, so connected accounts keep working. Sealing fails closed: if the secret service is unavailable the token is not stored. Five existing test files now mock the secret service and two storage assertions expect the sealed form (disclosed).
items.remaining: Existing plaintext tokens stay plaintext until each account is refreshed or reconnected; a one-off backfill needs the production secret service and was not run.

batches.family: Generic CRUD attribution fields and verified credits

items.explanation: The factory already refuses any key that is not a real column and any identity, tenancy, owner and lifecycle-time field. B92 widens the refused set to attribution and approval written under other spellings (createdById, approvedById, reviewedById, publishedById, verifiedById/Name/Date, approvedByName/Date, closedBy/ById, resolvedBy/ById, signedBy/ById, enteredBy), so the person and time of an act are always the server's record on all 98 factory routes; the factory and route suites pass.
items.remaining: A route that lists no writableFields (84 of the 98) still accepts any real, non-reserved column, including status, cost and outcome columns; each needs its own allow-list decided from what its screens send.

items.explanation: Verified on source in B92: DELETE no longer writes an invented archived value into a domain enum; a status column that cannot take it refuses generic deletion with a 403 that names the governed lifecycle action (supportsGenericArchive).
Verified on source in B92: the item PATCH parses a strict schema (no body copy), is owner-only under the caller's tenant context, and audits a change of sharing level with the previous and new level.

batches.family: Health-safety dashboard measures, dedicated queue key, archived employer input, verified credits

items.explanation: The measures are now taken on the dates the events happened: incidents are counted and the previous window compared by incident date, days without incident run from the latest incident date (null when none is on record, as before), inspections are those scheduled within the window up to now and the rate is completed over those, and the hazard trend compares hazards reported in the window with the same length before it instead of reading the number currently open. Fixed clean metrics on a failure and a constant training figure were already removed.
Timesheet ingest now refuses an archived employer (409) instead of continuing to take payroll input for it.
items.remaining: The generic employer delete still sets only status archived (no archived-at stamp) and does not check for open timesheet batches, contacts or communications; a governed archive action is needed.

batches.family: KPI target bounds, external refusal audit scope, profile roles

items.explanation: POST /api/targets now stores a calculation only as one named aggregation (sum, avg, count, min or max; strict, nothing else is kept) and refuses a target created with alertEnabled true, because no sender or recipient list exists to deliver an alert; it no longer stores a promise nothing keeps.
items.remaining: The summary route still does not apply the stored aggregation or data source; wiring it is a product change to the KPI engine.

items.explanation: A refusal for an actor who holds no representation authority is no longer written into the named organization's audit trail (it goes to the application log), so a signed-in stranger who names any organization id can no longer add rows to that organization's audit log; a refusal for an actor who does hold an authority is still audited there.
items.remaining: The route still opens the tenant transaction for the organization named by the caller before the grant is checked; the binder that requires an active membership applies only in canonical V2.

items.explanation: Verified on source in B94: the route no longer lists billing profiles; it answers the signed-in user's own roles from their live membership on GET and on POST (whose body is ignored), so there is no refused POST and no billing data.

batches.family: Durable records and access rules for report execution and knowledge-base reads

items.explanation: A successful execution now writes report.execute to the canonical audit log before the rows are returned (data source, field ids, filter count and row count, never the rows), where it was only a log line.
items.remaining: The route is still at the officer role title and no field-level authority limits which registry fields (member e-mail, claim rows) an officer may select.

items.explanation: A parent organization's knowledge-base row is now served to a child only when it is public or names the child in allowed_organizations (the access columns decide); the list search matches the title and summary the list returns, not the full content of rows whose content it does not show; and opening a document writes knowledge_base.read to the audit log before the content is returned. Exit-interview copies were already governed by the interview reader condition.
items.remaining: The routes still apply no union_knowledge_suite entitlement, because the same table serves organizations without that suite and which of them may read it is a product decision.

batches.family: Honest availability for an uncomputed store; public-address rule for a stored integration endpoint

items.explanation: The engagement route answers availability: not_computed when no snapshot exists, so an empty list is the absence of a measurement and not a finding that no member is disengaged.
items.remaining: Nothing computes engagement snapshots (computeMemberEngagement has no caller), and the executive summary and key-indicator disengaged-member counts still read the same empty store; a scheduled scorer is a product change.

items.explanation: An integration endpoint written through PATCH must now be a public http(s) address (the same rule as every other address the platform is told to call). Every read, update and delete of an integration configuration, and its audit record, now states inEffect: false with the reason, and the capability is recorded as NOT_IMPLEMENTED (UE-EXT-INTEGRATION-SYNC), so a change is no longer presented as having affected a synchronization. A creation path was deliberately not added: it would store more configuration that nothing consumes.
items.remaining: No synchronization runs from the configuration, so enabling an integration, a sync frequency or an endpoint change has no effect. The worker and its provider qualification are the missing capability.

batches.family: Pilot write audit, organization verification basis, KPI value freshness

items.explanation: withLockedPilotMutation takes an optional audit declaration from the mutation and, when something was actually written, commits the audit row in the same transaction as the locked update, under the owning organization (or the acting platform organization for an application not yet bound); a missing actor refuses the write. The artifact, intelligence and reference-profile POST handlers declare pilot.artifact_version.add, pilot.intelligence.add and pilot.reference_profile.snapshot. No audit row is written when a branch writes nothing. The mutation helper test and two route tests were extended or given the actor and audit mocks (disclosed).

Verification now requires the basis the administrator relied on (20 to 1000 characters) and keeps it in the audit record with the binding; a request without it is refused. The binding now rests on what the server can check, not only on the administrator's selection. bindPilotOrganization compares the applicant's contact e-mail with the target organization's active member addresses and the organization name the applicant gave with the organization's own name, records both results in the audit record, and refuses (409, nothing written) when neither links the applicant to the organization unless the administrator resubmits with acknowledgeUncorroborated, in which case the audit record states that the verification rests on the stated basis alone. The basis (at least 20 characters) was already required. Three tests added; the bind tests were adapted to the extra reads and the test double made awaitable after limit.
items.remaining: An organization with no member yet and a different name can still be verified on the administrator's basis, by design and explicitly recorded as uncorroborated.

items.explanation: The summary states which row a current value came from (valueBasis, asOf), treats a metric row whose period ended more than 120 days ago as no current value (stale: true, health no_data) instead of judging the target against it, and no longer reports the trend of a stale row.
items.remaining: Neither the declared data source nor the calculation is applied to the metric rows; the value is still the latest row of the same metric type text.

batches.family: Case authority for arbitration writes

items.explanation: Creating an arbitration now requires that the grievanceId in the body be a grievance of the caller's organization (assertOrganizationOwns) and that the case authority allow the caller to edit that case (owner, or a collaborator with editing permission); changing one re-checks the same authority against the row loaded under the update's lock, and the grievance an arbitration belongs to cannot be changed.
items.remaining: Reads of the collection and item still return every arbitration of the organization to a steward, and DELETE is not re-checked against the case; the generic factory has no per-row read hook for a kernel decision.

batches.family: Clause-library anonymized source projection across system-role list/search/compare

items.explanation: The system-role list, search and compare paths now apply a shared source-organization projection. For an anonymized or unclassified clause, cross-organization readers do not receive the source organization id/name; the source owner retains attribution. Search and compare explicitly select the anonymization flag instead of silently omitting it. A unit test covers the disclosure rule and a source contract asserts use in all three routes. The item GET now uses the same source projection and treats an unset anonymization flag as not permission to disclose the original employer; a route regression exercises this legacy-null case.
items.remaining: System-role access remains subject to the SQL sharing-authority predicate and its policy; native PG15/16 cross-tenant tests, real HTTP response checks, anonymization of free-text content, and independent review are not yet established. This correction does not qualify all cross-tenant reads.

batches.family: Smart onboarding lookup failures and fabricated national benchmarks

items.explanation: Federation, clause, peer and benchmark lookups now propagate storage failures instead of returning empty arrays that look like successful no-match results. Unknown organizations are rejected, while real empty datasets still return empty results. Tests distinguish those cases and verify propagation. National averages also no longer use invented fallback numbers or relabel peer averages as national figures: missing/failed/unmeasured CLC results return null, and empty peer counts do not yield NaN. A follow-up rejects invalid cached measurements, refuses an implicit guessed CLC endpoint (explicit HTTPS URL and key required), and skips a benchmark when no peer counts were measured. Regression cases cover invalid cache and empty peer measurements.

batches.family: PostgreSQL migrations: SCIM bearer token, SLA status clock, survey anonymity, decision owner

items.explanation: Platform 0049 adds claims.status_changed_at, kept by a BEFORE trigger that stamps creation and a real status change and ignores an edit that leaves the status alone, and an append-only claim_status_transitions history written by a SECURITY DEFINER trigger (cache 0039 leaves the application roles SELECT only). Every SLA reader (workflow engine, alerts, watchdog, breach score) starts the clock at slaClockStart: the last status change, else creation, and says which basis it used. Claims that predate the column are not backfilled from updated_at. Proven on native PostgreSQL 15 and 16 as union_eyes_runtime and union_eyes_system, including forged-transition denial and the trigger firing under forced row security.

The SCIM Users route now authenticates the identity provider by the organization's bearer token, not a browser session: only the SHA-256 is stored (platform 0048 has no bearer_token column and hashes a legacy plaintext one), the lookup is by hash with a constant-time compare, a disabled, revoked or expired configuration authenticates nothing, the token (not the path) decides the organization, and the surface is rate limited per client and refuses when the limiter is unavailable. A signed-in administrator issues, rotates and revokes the token at /api/enterprise/sso/scim-token (shown once, audited atomically). The SCIM prefix is public at the edge and the token route is not. Proven on native PostgreSQL 15 and 16 (hash and per-organization uniqueness, tenant isolation, system lookup by hash).
items.remaining: The route still offers only list and create: no get, replace, patch or delete of a user (so a deprovision cannot be sent), no groups, no ServiceProviderConfig, and no scim_events_log row per provisioning event; deprovision_action and the attribute mapping are stored but not consumed.

batches.family: Mandatory external-access audit, unrecorded sync outcome, unenforced settings, 501 for the absent DSR route, workbook peer floor

items.explanation: The external access decision is now written through persistAtomicAudit in its own tenant transaction and a failure throws, so the middleware answers 403 and the outside party receives nothing when the decision record could not be written; the legacy logger that logged and swallowed a failed insert is no longer on this path. A stranger who holds no authority is still not written into the named organization's trail.
items.remaining: The read or write that follows is still not recorded as its own event, the decision record commits before the read rather than in the same transaction, and a document request still writes a matter decision row and a document decision row.

items.explanation: performAuditedOperation reports whether the outcome record was written (outcomeReport.recorded), and the sync route returns auditOutcomeRecorded with the result, so a synchronization whose outcome row could not be written says so instead of looking fully audited; the intent row still precedes the effect.

The enterprise data subject request route no longer wraps the generic factory that refused every call with a 403 naming another route: it answers 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED for capability UE-PRIVACY-DSAR-WORKFLOW, as the privacy route does.
items.remaining: No request can still be received: the table has no organization column to scope a request to the institution that must answer it, which is a schema and ownership decision.

items.explanation: The settings save reports the stored-but-unenforced keys (session timeout, MFA, password policy, rate limit, webhook, IP and domain lists) as notEnforced with a message, so a saved value is not read as one in force.
items.remaining: No authentication, session, password, rate-limit or notification code reads these keys yet, and the settings screen does not yet display the notEnforced list.

items.explanation: A same-organization peer of a claimed workbook now needs a steward role in the claimed organization (hasRoleInOrganization), not just a membership, before the memory-holder routes admit it to read, change or delete the named people.
items.remaining: The named people still have no notice that they are recorded, and the PATCH and DELETE audit rows are written only when a row changed.

items.explanation: Credited from the B100 code change (commits 43cbe020f and f895de200): the invented national table is gone, an unavailable or invalid CLC measurement is null and is never replaced by a peer average, the endpoint must be an explicitly configured HTTPS URL, and a peer set with no positive member counts yields no average or percentile instead of 0 divided by 0. The existing tests assert nationalAverage null for an unset key, a 404, an invalid body, an invalid cache and a thrown error.

batches.family: Organization selection is audited before it takes effect

items.explanation: Selecting an organization to work in now leaves an organization.select audit record (actor, organization, and whether the authority was membership or platform administrator) written through the atomic audit before the session is rebound, the preference cookie is set or the organization is returned; if the record cannot be written the selection is refused (503 in legacy mode, an error in canonical mode). A platform administrator selecting an organization they hold no membership of is named as such. The selection record (B103) now names the organization the actor was working in before (from the session or provider), and the canonical selection records its outcome after the session store has been changed or has refused (organization.selected, organization.select_failed). An intent with no outcome is a selection that did not complete.
items.remaining: The session store cannot commit with an audit row, so the pair is two-phase; the legacy path keeps no server-side previous organization and records null.

batches.family: Social OAuth callback authenticity and cookie lifecycle

items.explanation: OAuth callback now validates state, signed-in user, active organization, platform, code and PKCE prerequisites before consuming temporary connection cookies. Invalid or forged callbacks cannot clear an unrelated pending connection. A valid provider denial consumes its matched flow, and valid credentials are exchanged only after cookie consumption. GET is required for provider redirects, while the credential-and-audit database transaction already exists. The validation helper passed 10/10 focused local behavioral cases; full Vitest, PostgreSQL and HTTP/browser qualification remain pending.

batches.family: F06 A1: audit-write contract, truthful route manifest, canonical audit visibility, representation protocol capability

items.explanation: The scanner no longer overstates. A generic CRUD route whose table is not OPERATIONAL (read from lib/api/crud-governance.ts, the one place that decides it) refuses every write, so it is reported as not mutating with a READ_ONLY audit class (54 routes); a route that reaches performAuditedOperation is reported INTENT_OUTCOME instead of ATOMIC_SERVICE (41 routes), because operation-audit.ts contains persistAtomicAudit and every route importing it was being counted atomic; and a handler-level requireSystemAdmin( or hasMinRole( is now seen as the ADMIN_AUTH or ROLE_AUTH guard it is (it was reported as a bare session check). Each rule is exercised on a synthetic tree.

The audits list and detail routes now read through lib/audit/audit-reader.ts in the caller's tenant transaction: the legacy audit_security.audit_logs always, and in canonical mode the hash-chained public.audit_logs that persistAtomicAudit actually writes (including the audit.entry.read record the detail route writes). Each entry says which store it came from; the canonical store records no severity or outcome, so those are null, not invented. No details, changes, addresses or session data are returned from either store, and the page is bounded.
items.remaining: Proven with mocked transactions only; the canonical read has not been run against the combined PostgreSQL database.

items.explanation: The representation protocol (administrator-saved, approved by someone other than its author, every change written with persistAtomicAudit) is now owned by a named capability, UE-REP-PROTOCOL-GOVERNANCE, recorded LIMITED with its files, evidence and limits. The frozen register entry is untouched.
items.remaining: The Gate 0B.2 ownership ratification is an institutional decision this change cannot make; the GET read is still logged by the API audit logger rather than recorded atomically.

items.explanation: The audit-write contract is now stated in one place: performAtomicAuditedOperation writes the change and a single hash-chained audit record in one tenant transaction (a failed audit write abandons the change; a failed change records nothing; afterCommit runs only after commit), and performAuditedOperation is documented and labelled INTENT_OUTCOME as the durable two-phase record for effects our transaction cannot reach. The manifest no longer declares the two-phase routes atomic. The platform feature-flag toggle, a pure database change, moved onto the atomic contract (an undefined flag is a 404 rather than an insert the runtime role may not make). The two database-only operations that were still two-phase, the CBA registry seed and the benchmark snapshot, now write the change and a single hash-chained audit record in one system-scope transaction (a failed audit write rolls the whole seed or snapshot back; the seed fails fast so a swallowed statement error cannot leave an aborted transaction reporting a partial result). performAtomicAuditedOperation and performAuditedOperation gain resultDetails, so the record carries what the work did.
items.remaining: Operations that act outside the database transaction stay durable two-phase records, labelled INTENT_OUTCOME in the route manifest rather than ATOMIC. Billing-cycle generation is finance-frozen and was not changed.

batches.family: F06 A2: mutation and mandatory audit record in one database transaction

items.explanation: Every review decision is now audited in the decision's transaction. A claimed assessment is audited against the claiming organization; an unclaimed prospect assessment against the organization the reviewing platform administrator is acting in (as for any platform operation); a reviewer acting in no organization gets a 409 and no decision is made unrecorded. The reviewer's summary text is not copied into the audit record. The existing test that pinned the absence of an audit was replaced (disclosed).

runReconciliation writes its completed and critical-variance audit records with persistAtomicAudit on the run's own transaction, and resolveException updates the exception and writes its record in one transaction (the notes stay on the exception row and only their length reaches the audit record). A failed audit write abandons the run or leaves the exception open, and a rolled-back run leaves no audit event. This changes audit atomicity only; no financial mandate, ledger effect or principal changed (the finance freeze stands).

batches.family: F06 A4: a state, status or audit record names an outcome only when the system performed or can show it

items.explanation: The transition no longer says an effect happened when it did not. Every state that writes a contract, invoice or subscription (contract_sent, contract_signed, invoice_issued, subscription_active) is refused with 409 and nothing changed when its billing account, contract or active plan is missing, where it used to push a "staged only" note and still commit the new state, status, score history and audit row. contract_signed needs counterpartAcceptance (who accepted for the other party, their role, the channel and an evidence reference), is refused unless a contract exists and is awaiting acceptance, and records the acceptance, the recording administrator and the fact that it was recorded by a platform operator in the contract; a replay does not overwrite it. An invoice is issued only against an accepted (active) contract. A pilot status of approved, active or completed is written only once platform-approved commercial terms exist. Seven existing tests were adapted (staged-only expectations became refusals) and eleven added; the admin UI collects the acceptance. Disclosed adaptations: the mocked state order in the route test now includes approved, pilot_active and pilot_complete.
items.remaining: The counterpart's acceptance is evidence an administrator records (a document or envelope reference), not a signature the system verified. Provider-verified e-signature, or an authenticated counterpart acceptance step, needs a signing provider and a counterpart identity that this release does not have.

items.explanation: A step is marked complete only when the organization's own data shows it: the organization record exists, a member other than the caller exists, a member other than the caller holds a role above member, a collective agreement is stored, an employer exists, an integration is configured, and an export was audited (a new hasAuditedAction reads both audit stores and excludes rejected, unavailable and request-only actions). Otherwise the PATCH returns 409 naming what is missing and writes nothing; reopening needs no evidence; the counts are recorded in the audit row, no row content. The evidence SQL was checked against the real PostgreSQL 16 schema. Two tests added; existing tests adapted to a mocked verifier.
items.remaining: A configured integration only exists as stored configuration (UE-EXT-INTEGRATION-SYNC is NOT_IMPLEMENTED), so integrations-configured evidences configuration, not a working integration.

items.explanation: The event and its audit row are written only after the organization's membership data shows the milestone: org_created needs the organization to exist, user_invited a named target that is a member of this organization, and role_assigned a named target that is an active member holding that role. An unverified milestone returns 409 and writes neither the event nor the audit row; the event is stamped with what it was verified against and the audit row carries the evidence. Two tests added.
items.remaining: user_invited is evidenced by the member row, not by a sent invitation, because an invitation record is not a single governed table.

items.explanation: Only platform-administrator authority (isPlatformAdminUser) opens the cross-organization overview; an officer role title in the platform organization no longer does. The read is paged (default 25, at most 100, ordered), takes three queries for the whole page instead of three per organization, and is recorded with performAtomicAuditedOperation in the system scope with the page it returned; a read that cannot be audited returns nothing. The test file was rewritten (disclosed): the old legacy-platform-organization expectations were removed, and tests added for attribution between organizations, bounds, the audit and an audit failure.
items.remaining: The platform dashboard shows the first page only; a pager is a UI follow-up.

items.explanation: A payroll run is sealed (posted) only after a remittance package has been generated for it, in the same transaction, so a posted run always means something was done with its amounts; with none the seal is refused (409) and nothing is written. The compliance event and the audit record name the remittance run, the event summary says the system makes no payment or ledger entry, and the response returns the remittance id. No finance mandate, principal or amount logic was changed.
items.remaining: Payment and ledger settlement are not performed by this system; the posted state means sealed after remittance, as the event states.

items.explanation: Every provider list, create, update and delete response, and the create and update audit records, now states inEffect: false with the reason, and the capability is recorded as NOT_IMPLEMENTED (UE-SSO-SIGN-IN), so a configured provider is no longer reported as though it governed sign-in.
items.remaining: No sign-in, token-exchange, provisioning or SCIM code reads the stored provider; the consumer needs the identity-provider protocol work and a real provider to qualify against.

batches.family: F06 A3: each state change of a multi-step operation is recorded for what it is, with the durable record that leads to it

items.explanation: Source seeding is atomic (see above). Ingestion runs and extraction call external sources and an AI provider across many statements, so they cannot share one transaction and are no longer described as atomic: the manifest labels them INTENT_OUTCOME, and the outcome record now names the durable rows the run wrote (job ids and counts; extraction run ids and counts), so the audit trail leads to them.
items.remaining: Ingestion and extraction remain two-phase by nature; no provider was exercised in this batch.

items.explanation: The provider call stays inside the durable intent and outcome record, but the connection's own state change is now a tenant transaction that also writes its audit record: calendar_sync.connection.state_synced on success and calendar_sync.connection.sync_failed, with the connection marked failed, when the provider fails (previously a failure left the connection unchanged and unrecorded). A state change whose audit record cannot be written fails the sync instead of reporting it synced.
items.remaining: Events imported or exported before a later provider failure remain; the failure is recorded, not rolled back at the provider.

items.explanation: Revocation spans sessions, the platform-auth membership and the local row, which cannot share a transaction, so the attempt is made durable before any store is touched (member.access.deactivate_attempt or delete_attempt) and the outcome is recorded atomically with the local status change as before. A process that stops part-way leaves a visible attempt with no outcome, and a repeat is idempotent. Unlike reactivation, a revocation whose attempt cannot be recorded is still carried out, because denying access is the safe direction; the outcome record then says attemptRecorded: false and the result reports intentRecorded.
items.remaining: Three stores are still updated separately; a failed step still returns 502 and is completed by a retry.

items.explanation: The initiation record now says a payment was opened, and what the provider then did is recorded as its own state change in its own transaction: dues.payment_provider_intent_linked with the processor id, dues.payment_cancelled with the reason (provider_intent_not_created, superseded_by_new_balance). A cancellation that cannot be written is logged, never discarded, and leaves the row pending, which is safe because a repeat reuses an open payment of the same amount and the provider call is idempotent on the payment id. A payment whose intent the provider created is no longer cancelled when only the local link failed (that left a chargeable intent whose settlement would be refused): it stays pending and a repeat reuses it. Four real-SQL tests added. No finance mandate, amount, principal or settlement logic was changed.
items.remaining: The provider call is still outside the transaction by nature.

items.explanation: The two effects are separated and each is recorded for what it is. Removal from the platform is a durable intent and outcome (with whether it was already gone); the row then reads deleted in one transaction with social.post.deleted. A platform failure now returns 502 PLATFORM_REMOVAL_FAILED with the row still published (true: the post is still live); a failure of the local step returns 502 LOCAL_STATE_PENDING, never "deleted", and repeating the deletion completes it because a platform answer that the post is already gone counts as removed. deletePost keeps its contract for other callers.
items.remaining: The already-removed detection reads the platform error text, since the platform clients expose no typed not-found.
